Iterate based on real usage and forward-test complex skills.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2852:- Name the skill folder exactly after the skill name.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2856:Skip this step only when the skill's usage patterns are already clearly understood. It remains valuable even when working with an existing skill.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2858:To create an effective skill, clearly understand concrete examples of how the skill will be used. This understanding can come from either direct user examples or generated examples that are validated with user feedback.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2860:For example, when building an image-editor skill, relevant questions include:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2862:- \"What functionality should the image-editor skill support? Editing, rotating, anything else?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2863:- \"Can you give some examples of how this skill would be used?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2864:- \"I can imagine users asking for things like 'Remove the red-eye from this image' or 'Rotate this image'. Are there other ways you imagine this skill being used?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2865:- \"What would a user say that should trigger this skill?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2866:- \"Where should I create this skill? If you do not have a preference, I will place it in `$CODEX_HOME/skills` (or `~/.codex/skills` when `CODEX_HOME` is unset) so Codex can discover it automatically.\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2870:Conclude this step when there is a clear sense of the functionality the skill should support.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2874:To turn concrete examples into an effective skill, analyze each example by:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2879:Example: When building a `pdf-editor` skill to handle queries like \"Help me rotate this PDF,\" the analysis shows:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2882:2. A `scripts/rotate_pdf.py` script would be helpful to store in the skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2884:Example: When designing a `frontend-webapp-builder` skill for queries like \"Build me a todo app\" or \"Build me a dashboard to track my steps,\" the analysis shows:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2887:2. An `assets/hello-world/` template containing the boilerplate HTML/React project files would be helpful to store in the skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2889:Example: When building a `big-query` skill to handle queries like \"How many users have logged in today?\" the analysis shows:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2892:2. A `references/schema.md` file documenting the table schemas would be helpful to store in the skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2894:To establish the skill's contents, analyze each concrete example to create a list of the reusable resources to include: scripts, references, and assets.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2898:At this point, it is time to actually create the skill.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2900:Skip this step only if the skill being developed already exists. In this case, continue to the next step.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2902:Before running `init_skill.py`, ask where the user wants the skill created. If they do not specify a location, default to `$CODEX_HOME/skills`; when `CODEX_HOME` is unset, fall back to `~/.codex/skills` so the skill is auto-discovered.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2904:When creating a new skill from scratch, always run the `init_skill.py` script. The script conveniently generates a new template skill directory that automatically includes everything a skill requires, making the skill creation process much more efficient and reliable.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2909:scripts/init_skill.py <skill-name> --path <output-directory> [--resources scripts,references,assets] [--examples]\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2915:scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path \"${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2916:scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path \"${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills\" --resources scripts,references\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2917:scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path ~/work/skills --resources scripts --examples\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2922:- Creates the skill directory at the specified path\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2930:Generate `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt` by reading the skill, then pass them as `--interface key=value` to `init_skill.py` or regenerate with:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2933:scripts/generate_openai_yaml.py <path/to/skill-folder> --interface key=value\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2940:When editing the (newly-generated or existing) skill, remember that the skill is being created for another instance of Codex to use. Include information that would be beneficial and non-obvious to Codex. Consider what procedural knowledge, domain-specific details, or reusable assets would help another Codex instance execute these tasks more effectively.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2942:After substantial revisions, or if the skill is particularly tricky, you should use subagents to forward-test the skill on realistic tasks or artifacts. When doing so, pass the artifact under validation rather than your diagnosis of what is wrong, and keep the prompt generic enough that success depends on transferable reasoning rather than hidden ground truth.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2946:To begin implementation, start with the reusable resources identified above: `scripts/`, `references/`, and `assets/` files. Note that this step may require user input. For example, when implementing a `brand-guidelines` skill, the user may need to provide brand assets or templates to store in `assets/`, or documentation to store in `references/`.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2950:If you used `--examples`, delete any placeholder files that are not needed for the skill. Only create resource directories that are actually required.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2960:- `name`: The skill name\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2961:- `description`: This is the primary triggering mechanism for your skill, and helps Codex understand when to use the skill.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2964:  - Example description for a `docx` skill: \"Comprehensive document creation, editing, and analysis with support for tracked changes, comments, formatting preservation, and text extraction. /home/jbb/.codex/skills/screen-content-planner/SKILL.md\"`\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3387:description: Turn one product analysis card, implementation plan, UX analysis, or equivalent planning artifact into a complete screen-content plan for future visual mockups. Use when Codex needs to determine which screens are needed, what each screen must contain, what app language, platform format, product wording, data, states, and missing information are required before a separate mockup-generation skill begins. Do not use for generating visual mockups, styling systems, image assets, or implementation code.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3396:This skill is the first step in a two-skill workflow:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3398:1. This skill defines screen scope, content, data, states, reuse constraints, and unresolved blockers.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3399:2. A later visual mockup skill turns the plan into mockups.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3429:5. **Map planned behavior.** Use the provided implementation or product plan to identify workflows, states, roles, data entities, edge cases, failure modes, and permission differences that need screen coverage.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3432:8. **Review wording for production readiness.** Ensure labels, headings, empty states, errors, CTAs, helper text, and status messages are written for end users, not developers or implementation teams.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3434:10. **Prepare the handoff.** End with a clean handoff note for the later visual mockup skill, without doing visual design work.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3456:Do not ask for visual style details such as color palette, typography, illustration direction, spacing, motion, or high-fidelity layout preferences. Those belong to the later mockup creation skill.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3464:Use wording that a real end user can understand in the application language. Avoid implementation wording, internal team shorthand, database names, component names, raw enum values, route names, debug labels, placeholder text, and developer instructions unless the product itself is for developers and the source explicitly requires that vocabulary.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3552:- Ensure every wording item is preserve.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3617:- User-facing wording is production-ready, in the application language, and free of development jargon, -->\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4:Ici, on a besoin de créer un skill qui va prendre le résultat du skill qu'on avait créé qui s'appelle Screen Content Planner, corrigé d'une bloat analysis éventuellement. En tout cas, ça prend une description de skill et enfin, ça prend une description de screen, pardon, et ça les transforme en mock-up visuel. Ce que ça fait, c'est que si jamais c'est une technologie web, on les fait directement, en fait, quoi qu'il arrive, en fait, on les fait en HTML et CSS. Et il faut bien que le skill, avant de générer les screens, il fasse une analyse complète des styles avec les couleurs, les border radius. En fait, il faut réutiliser ce qu'il y a dans Frontend skill pour pouvoir faire une analyse du design qu'on a dans l'application pour que les mock-ups, ils soient cohérents avec ce qu'on a déjà dans l'application. Et ensuite, ce qu'il faut que ça fasse, c'est que ça, du coup, ça génère les fichiers HTML et CSS, le CSS séparé du HTML à chaque fois. Chaque screen, il est dans son fichier HTML et chaque fichier HTML, il a son fichier CSS. Et ensuite, ce qu'on fait, c'est qu'on render avec le format d'image correct qui correspond à ce qu'on est en train de faire. Donc, par exemple, si c'est une application mobile en mode portrait, il faut qu'on fasse un render dans du browser en 9 16e et qu'on fasse ensuite une capture d'image et qu'on construise un carrousel dans la carte pour pouvoir montrer tous les mock-ups dans un carrousel. C'est aussi important que dans le skill, il y ait les règles de formatting qu'on a pour décision OS. Et ça veut dire qu'à chaque fois, je veux que les outputs soient créés avec les règles de formatting. Donc, ça veut dire que nos règles de formatting, il faut qu'on les ajoute à chaque skill qui est une tâche que tu dois faire alternative. Non, non, oublie cette tâche, je veux la faire moi-même. En tout cas, dans le skill que tu crées, il faudra mettre les règles de formatting et les règles de formatting, du coup, c'est les règles de formatting des cartes. C'est-à-dire que quand output du markdown, il faut que les titres, ils aient une lettre, que les sous-titres, ils aient une lettre un numéro, que les bullet points, elles aient des numéros, il faut que chaque section, elle soit séparée par un HR et il faut qu'il y ait du bold et des bactics.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:7:<!-- decision-os:note {\"id\":\"codex-codex-skill-1783493766495-deea83eb-line-1\",\"timestamp\":\"2026-07-08T06:56:08.973Z\",\"status\":\"running\",\"codexRunId\":\"codex-skill-1783493766495-deea83eb\",\"codexLine\":\"1\",\"codexKind\":\"run_status\",\"codexEventType\":\"thread.started\"} -->\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:12:<!-- decision-os:note {\"id\":\"codex-codex-skill-1783493766495-deea83eb-line-2\",\"timestamp\":\"2026-07-08T06:56:08.974Z\",\"status\":\"running\",\"codexRunId\":\"codex-skill-1783493766495-deea83eb\",\"codexLine\":\"2\",\"codexKind\":\"run_status\",\"codexEventType\":\"turn.started\"} -->\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:17:<!-- decision-os:note {\"id\":\"codex-codex-skill-1783493766495-deea83eb-line-3\",\"timestamp\":\"2026-07-08T06:56:24.973Z\",\"status\":\"Codex message\",\"codexRunId\":\"codex-skill-1783493766495-deea83eb\",\"codexLine\":\"3\",\"codexKind\":\"agent_message\",\"codexEventType\":\"item.completed\",\"codexItemId\":\"item_0\"} -->\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:19:I’ll use the decision-os note treatment workflow, scoped to the single thread and card you named. This skill should be used when users want to create a new skill (or update an existing skill) that extends Codex's capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, or tool integrations.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:259:  short-description: Create or update a skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:264:This skill provides guidance for creating effective skills.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:304:You may use subagents during iteration to validate whether a skill works on realistic tasks or whether a suspected problem is real. This is most useful when you want an independent pass on the skill's behavior, outputs, or failure modes after a revision.  Only do this when it is possible to start new subagents.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:306:When using subagents for validation, treat that as an evaluation surface. The goal is to learn whether the skill generalizes, not whether another agent can reconstruct the answer from leaked context.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:312:Every skill consists of a required SKILL.md file and optional bundled resources:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:315:skill-name/\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:322:│   └── openai.yaml - UI metadata for skill lists and chips\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:333:- **Frontmatter** (YAML): Contains `name` and `description` fields. These are the only fields that Codex reads to determine when the skill gets used, thus it is very important to be clear and comprehensive in describing what the skill is, and when it should be used.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:334:- **Body** (Markdown): Instructions and guidance for using the skill. Only loaded AFTER the skill triggers (if at all).\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:338:- UI-facing metadata for skill lists and chips\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:340:- Create: human-facing `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt` by reading the skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:341:- Generate deterministically by passing the values as `--interface key=value` to `scripts/generate_openai_yaml.py` or `scripts/init_skill.py`\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:366:- **Avoid duplication**: Information should live in either SKILL.md or references files, not both. Prefer references files for detailed information unless it's truly core to the skill—this keeps SKILL.md lean while making information discoverable without hogging the context window. Keep only essential procedural instructions and workflow guidance in SKILL.md; move detailed reference material, schemas, and examples to references files.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:372:- **When to include**: When the skill needs files that will be used in the final output\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:379:A skill should only contain essential files that directly support its functionality. Do NOT create extraneous documentation or auxiliary files, including:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:387:The skill should only contain the information needed for an AI agent to do the job at hand. It should not contain auxiliary context about the process that went into creating it, setup and testing procedures, user-facing documentation, etc. Creating additional documentation files just adds clutter and confusion.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:394:2. **SKILL.md body** - When skill triggers (<5k words)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:399:Keep SKILL.md body to the essentials and under 500 lines to minimize context bloat. Split content into separate files when approaching this limit. When splitting out content into other files, it is very important to reference them from SKILL.md and describe clearly when to read them, to ensure the reader of the skill knows they exist and when to use them.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:401:**Key principle:** When a skill supports multiple variations, frameworks, or options, keep only the core workflow and selection guidance in SKILL.md. Move variant-specific details (patterns, examples, configuration) into separate reference files.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:427:bigquery-skill/\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:438:Similarly, for skills supporting multiple frameworks or variants, organize by variant:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:481:1. Understand the skill with concrete examples\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:482:2. Plan reusable skill contents (scripts, references, assets)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:483:3. Initialize the skill (run init_skill.py)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:484:4. Edit the skill (implement resources and write SKILL.md)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:485:5. Validate the skill (run quick_validate.py)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:486:6. Iterate based on real usage and forward-test complex skills.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:496:- Name the skill folder exactly after the skill name.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:500:Skip this step only when the skill's usage patterns are already clearly understood. It remains valuable even when working with an existing skill.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:502:To create an effective skill, clearly understand concrete examples of how the skill will be used. This understanding can come from either direct user examples or generated examples that are validated with user feedback.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:504:For example, when building an image-editor skill, relevant questions include:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:506:- \"What functionality should the image-editor skill support? Editing, rotating, anything else?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:507:- \"Can you give some examples of how this skill would be used?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:508:- \"I can imagine users asking for things like 'Remove the red-eye from this image' or 'Rotate this image'. En tout cas, ça prend une description de skill et enfin, ça prend une description de screen, pardon, et ça les transforme en mock-up visuel. Ce que ça fait, c'est que si jamais c'est une technologie web, on les fait directement, en fait, quoi qu'il arrive, en fait, on les fait en HTML et CSS. Et il faut bien que le skill, avant de générer les screens, il fasse une analyse complète des styles avec les couleurs, les border radius. En fait, il faut réutiliser ce qu'il y a dans Frontend skill pour pouvoir faire une analyse du design qu'on a dans l'application pour que les mock-ups, ils soient cohérents avec ce qu'on a déjà dans l'application. Et ensuite, ce qu'il faut que ça fasse, c'est que ça, du coup, ça génère les fichiers HTML et CSS, le CSS séparé du HTML à chaque fois. Chaque screen, il est dans son fichier HTML et chaque fichier HTML, il a son fichier CSS. Et ensuite, ce qu'on fait, c'est qu'on render avec le format d'image correct qui correspond à ce qu'on est en train de faire. Donc, par exemple, si c'est une application mobile en mode portrait, il faut qu'on fasse un render dans du browser en 9 16e et qu'on fasse ensuite une capture d'image et qu'on construise un carrousel dans la carte pour pouvoir montrer tous les mock-ups dans un carrousel. C'est aussi important que dans le skill, il y ait les règles de formatting qu'on a pour décision OS. A clear Section A object list for logs, goal, tasks, work, mockups, analyses, learning, questions, proposals, reports, and specs.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:736:/home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os/.decision-os/threads/tasks-system/thread-card-codex-skill-1783443352880-df6faf0b.md:624:.decision-os/cards/tasks-system/card-905302cd-3cfa-41d7-8e0d-a3ffd55a5429.md:22:4. **Different UX per object:** each object gets a purpose-shaped surface instead of a repeated section layout: logs use a trace console, goal uses an object map, tasks use a queue board, work uses a diff viewer, mockups use a capture gallery, analyses use an evidence matrix, learning uses a promotion path, questions use an operator gate, proposals use a comparison view, reports use an outcome digest, and specs use a contract editor.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:737:/home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os/.decision-os/threads/tasks-system/thread-card-codex-skill-1783443352880-df6faf0b.md:626:.decision-os/cards/tasks-system/card-905302cd-3cfa-41d7-8e0d-a3ffd55a5429.md:30:![Tasks object mockup](.decision-os/ui-mockups/goal-object-tasks.png)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:738:/home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os/.decision-os/threads/tasks-system/thread-card-codex-skill-1783443352880-df6faf0b.md:627:.decision-os/cards/tasks-system/card-905302cd-3cfa-41d7-8e0d-a3ffd55a5429.md:44:![Global goal tasks tab](.decis, task cards, image carousels, HTML card assets, and report mockups can all live inside the workspace. [A2, A6, B8, C2]\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:3748:/home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os/.decision-os/cards/skills/card-1ed7edae-2bff-4f0e-a922-1bb57a0b6e93.md:3:1. **Skill purpose:** Create a Codex skill that turns an analysis card into a complete screen-content plan for future mockups.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:3749:/home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os/.decision-os/cards/skills/card-1ed7edae-2bff-4f0e-a922-1bb57a0b6e93.md:4:2. **Primary outcome:** The skill must determine which screens are needed, what each screen must contain, and what source data is still missing before visual mockup creation begins.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:3750:/home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os/.decision-os/cards/skills/card-1ed7edae-2bff-4f0e-a922-1bb57a0b6e93.md:5:3. **Workflow position:** This is the first skill in a two-skill workflow. Correction And Evidence Boundary\n\n1. **Correction.** The previous update wrongly replaced earlier findings instead of merging them. `ticket-solver`, `openticket`, `improveticket`, `product-analysis`, and the executor skills should not have been removed from the inventory.\n2. **Merged source set.** This card now combines local installed Codex skills from `/home/jbb/.codex/skills`, DroidFleet repo-local skills from `/home/jbb/dev/DroidFleet/.codex/skills`, DroidFleet Factory prompts and pipeline rules from `/home/jbb/dev/DroidFleet/factory`, and executor skills from `/home/jbb/dev/AgentSkills` and `/home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os/.skills`.\n3. **Classification rule.** Skills are not all the same kind of planner. Some normalize a goal into a ticket, some create a task list, some decompose product work into child issues, some produce implementation DAGs, and some execute after planning.\n\n---\n\n## B. Local Codex Skills Retained From First Pass\n\n1. **`openticket`.** Planning skill for a broad operator-reported problem. It performs code-first static analysis, drafts `REQ-*` requirements, scope, codebase impact intent, dependency blockers, an `Ideal Control-flow DAG`, and acceptance checks, then opens a GitLab issue only after operator approval.\n2. **`improveticket`.** Planning skill for an existing weak GitLab issue. It rewrites the issue into the OpenTicket structure, asks for operator approval, updates the issue, applies factory-actionable labels, and removes `improve`.\n3. **`product-analysis`.** Pre-planning analysis skill. It maps a goal to affected workflow, actor, linked specs, missing specs, and spec gaps from code evidence. It explicitly does not recommend an implementation path or approval gate.\n4. **`ticket-solver`.** Execution-first DroidFleet skill. It solves an existing GitLab ticket end to end, but it still creates a working document and full control-flow DAG before implementation. It belongs after a ticket exists, not at the start of a broad goal.\n5. **`executor-precheck`.** Checks whether an operator goal has enough approved `Specs`, `Data Model`, `Runtime State`, repo facts, and scope boundary before stack planning.\n6. **`executor-stack`.** Analyzes specs/data/runtime, identifies `Root Blocks`, validates stack choices, creates an agnostic directory scaffold, and asks blocking operator questions.\n7. **`executor-spec`.** Builds the `Master Ledger`: domains, one test suite per spec, inputs, effects, helpers, screens/pages, components, state, control-flow entries, unresolved questions, and spec candidates. This is the strongest executor-side `goal -> implementation structure` splitter.\n8. **`executor-implement`.** Implementation skill that consumes the `Master Ledger`. It should not infer architecture or split a broad goal by itself.\n9. **`decision-os-treat-open-notes`.** Inbox-treatment skill for answering operator notes and updating cards/threads. It can perform ledger work, but it is not a general planning splitter.\n\n---\n\n## C. DroidFleet OpenSpec Planning Skills\n\n1. **`openspec-explore`.** Thinking and investigation mode. It reads code, compares options, surfaces risks, and can capture decisions into OpenSpec artifacts, but it does not implement.\n2. **`openspec-new-change`.** Starts a new change from a goal or change name. It creates `openspec/changes/<name>/`, shows artifact status, and displays the first artifact instructions.\n3. **`openspec-continue-change`.** Progresses one artifact at a time. In the spec-driven schema, the sequence is `proposal.md -> specs/<capability>/spec.md -> design.md -> tasks.md`; `tasks.md` is the checkboxed implementation task list.\n4. **`openspec-ff-change`.** Fast-forwards artifact creation until implementation is ready. This is the strongest OpenSpec `goal -> task list` skill because it creates the required artifacts in dependency order, including `tasks.md`.\n5. **`openspec-apply-change`.** Executes tasks from an OpenSpec change. It is implementation, not planning, but it consumes the task list.\n6. **`openspec-verify-change`.** Verifies implementation against `tasks`, `specs`, and `design`. It is planning-adjacent quality control, not a splitter.\n\n---\n\n## D. DroidFactory Planning Roles\n\n1. **`ticket/improver`.** Normalizes an existing weak issue into a factory-ready ticket. Required body structure: `Problem Report`, `REQ-###`, `Scope`, `Codebase Impact Intent`, `Dependency Blockers`, `Ideal Control-flow DAG`, and `Acceptance`. It classifies the issue as `feature` or `bug`; the orchestrator then applies the first pipeline labels.\n2. **`product/analyzer`.** Turns a vague product request into a production-grade problem definition with problem statement, goals, non-goals, scope boundaries, key unknowns, and operator-dependent integrations.\n3. **`product/rfc-writer`.** Produces the implementation path: proposed solution, alternatives, tradeoffs, integration strategy, and mock/live switches for operator-dependent integrations.\n4. **`product/architect`.** Defines components, boundaries, contracts, integration switches, failure handling, observability, and rollout assumptions.\n5. **`product/prd-writer`.** Converts approved product architecture into functional requirements, non-functional requirements, acceptance criteria, operator enablement, and release quality expectations.\n6. **`product/decomposer`.** Splits an approved product ticket into child epic tickets labeled `pipeline:epic`, `epic:research`, and `status:todo`.\n7. **`epic/analyzer`.** Converts an epic body into hard specs, intent interpretation, existing data model constraints, downstream execution contract, and proven gaps.\n8. **`epic/architect`.** Produces the epic implementation plan: data model deltas, module decomposition, helper extraction, integration points, dependency injection boundaries, test strategy, and ordered phases.\n9. **`epic/quality-planner`.** Red-teams `Epic Architecture`, reduces over-engineering, corrects factorization, and defines quality gates before decomposition.\n10. **`epic/decomposer`.** Splits corrected epic architecture into child feature issues labeled `pipeline:feature`, `feat:plan`, and `status:todo`. Each child issue contains problem statement, `REQ-*`, scope, codebase impact, dependency metadata, and acceptance criteria.\n11. **`feature/analyzer`.** Maps feature intent to codebase surface area and produces evidence-backed task breakdown, risks, planner TODOs, planner decisions, and recommended implementation order.\n12. **`feature/planner`.** Produces the implementation plan for one feature issue: `Spec`, `Codebase Impact Intent`, `Dependency Blockers`, and `Ideal Control-flow DAG`. It does not create child issues.\n13. **`bug/rca`.** Produces the pre-fix bug plan: reproduction status, code-path trace, root cause, fix scope, mandatory fix DAG, spec-change check, factorization check, regression test plan, and fixer checklist.\n14. **`refactor/analyzer`.** Ranks top refactor candidates and selects the primary set for the run. It is a planning role for refactor work, but it does not create issues.\n15. **`prototype/delivery-planner`.** Converts a design package into a delivery plan with milestones, backlog decomposition, dependency map, risk register, and validation gates.\n\n---\n\n## E. DroidFactory Pipeline Labels\n\n1. **Feature pipeline.** `pipeline:feature` stages include `feat:plan`, `feat:implement`, `feat:audit`, plus recovery stages such as `feat:commit_fix`, `feat:test_fix`, and `feat:merge_solve`. The first actionable planning stage is `feature/planner`.\n2. **Bug pipeline.** `pipeline:bug` starts with `bug:rca`, then `bug:fix`, `bug:audit`, and `bug:archive`, with similar recovery stages. The planning stage is `bug/rca`.\n3. **Product pipeline.** `pipeline:product` includes `analysis`, `research`, `rfc`, `architecture`, `prd`, red-team stages, and `decompose`. The decomposition stage creates child epics.\n4. **Epic pipeline.** `pipeline:epic` includes `research`, `analyze`, `architecture`, `quality`, `decompose`, and `review`. The decomposition stage creates child feature tickets.\n5. **Research pipeline.** `pipeline:research` includes `scan`, `summarize`, `deep_dive`, and `conclude`. It is evidence-building rather than implementation task splitting.\n6. **Refactor pipeline.** `pipeline:refactor` includes `analyze`, `implement`, and `audit`. The analyzer selects concrete code hygiene targets.\n\n---\n\n## F. Extracted Decision Information\n\n1. **Best OpenSpec goal-to-task skill.** Use `openspec-ff-change` when the desired output is a complete OpenSpec artifact set ending in `tasks.md`.\n2. **Best local ticket planner.** Use `openticket` for a broad operator problem that should become a GitLab issue after approval.\n3. **Best local issue-upgrader.** Use `improveticket` when an existing issue is weak and needs OpenTicket structure plus factory labels after approval.\n4. **Best Factory issue normalizer.** Use `ticket/improver` when DroidFactory should non-interactively normalize an `improve` issue and classify it for the feature or bug pipeline.\n5. **Best Factory product-to-work splitter.** Use `product/decomposer` to split an approved product ticket into epics, then `epic/decomposer` to split corrected epic architecture into feature tickets.\n6. **Best single-feature planner.** Use `feature/analyzer` before `feature/planner` when the feature needs grounded codebase surface mapping before the implementation DAG.\n7. **Best bug planner.** Use `bug/rca`, because it produces fix scope, fix DAG, regression test plan, and fixer checklist before implementation.\n8. **Where `ticket-solver` belongs.** `ticket-solver` remains important, but it is a downstream solver for an existing ticket. It should consume a prepared ticket, create the working DAG, implement, test, and report evidence.\n9. **Executor vs Factory distinction.** Executor skills build a local `Master Ledger` implementation scaffold. DroidFactory skills operate through GitLab issues and labels as the workflow state machine.\n10. **Correct broad-goal chain in DroidFactory.** `ticket/improver -> product/analyzer/RFC/architecture/PRD -> product/decomposer -> epic/analyzer/architect/quality-planner -> epic/decomposer -> feature/analyzer -> feature/planner -> feature/implementer`.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

````text
# decision-os Agent Instructions

## Language Policy

- All agent responses MUST be written in English only.
- The operator may speak or write in French; do not mirror the operator's language.
- decision-os `# AGENT` thread replies must be in English, even when the corresponding `# OPERATOR` note is French.
- Do not write French acknowledgements such as `Traité`; use English equivalents such as `Treated`.

## KNOWLEDGE

### Anti Specs

- **Rule.** Never write anti-specs: generic process claims that spend operator tokens and attention without adding a concrete requirement, constraint, decision, evidence, or action.
- **Don't.** `Good PRDs do not exist to create paperwork. They align teams around the customer problem, goals, requirements, risks, constraints, dependencies, and success measures before execution.`
- **Do.** `PRD purpose: capture the requested decision, user need, current technical context, current UX context, constraints, evidence, risks, options, recommendation, acceptance criteria, and next operator gate.`

### No Suppositions

- **Rule.** Never write suppositions when the answer can be verified from the repo, tools, CLI, docs, runtime state, or available evidence. Search, inspect, run the relevant command, and report the finding.
- **Don't.** `If ledger-cli does not expose that query, then the missing piece is a CLI contract.`
- **Do.** `Finding: ledger-cli exposes no zone-context query. Evidence: rg found no command handler or help entry for zone context under cli/. Required action: add the ledger-cli query contract.`
- **Blocker.** When evidence cannot be obtained, state the verified blocker and ask one concrete operator question. Do not replace missing evidence with conditional analysis.

### No Or In Plans

- **Rule.** Never leave unresolved alternatives with `or` in a final implementation plan, recommendation, acceptance criteria, or `# AGENT` answer. Pick the single best solution from the evidence. Options are valid only inside explicit questions to the operator.
- **Don't.** `Add headers or query params: x-ledger-id, x-thread-id, x-card-id, x-note-id, x-queue-codex.`
- **Do.** `Add required headers to /api/voice-upload: x-ledger-id, x-thread-id, x-card-id, x-note-id, x-queue-codex.`

### Formatting Contract

1. **Headings:** use `H2` card sections with uppercase letters: `## A. Scope`, `## B. Contract`, `## C. Acceptance Criteria`.
2. **Dividers:** put `---` between card sections.
3. **Lists:** write section content as numbered list items: `1.`, `2.`, `3.`.
4. **Bold:** use **bold** for the important words that carry the point.
5. **Backticks:** use `backticks` for technical, secondary, exact, or literal terms: file paths, routes, config keys, commands, IDs, statuses, branch names, code symbols, and literal values.

## decision-os Server Procedure

decision-os serves the active `.decision-os` workspace by resolving the workspace root from the process
current working directory. Always start the server from the target project workspace, not from the
decision-os repo, unless the operator explicitly wants to inspect the repo's own ledgers.

For this decision-os repo workspace, use port `50150`. Port `4174` is registered to
`Ardaria_57` in multiterm state; do not start this repo on `4174`.

```bash
cd /home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os
setsid sh -c 'cd /home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os && exec env PORT=50150 /home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os/bin/decision-os-server.mjs >> /tmp/decision-os-50150.log 2>&1' </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &

Expected routes for decision-os:

http://127.0.0.1:50150/specs
http://127.0.0.1:50150/data

## Background Launch Rules

- Use the repo launcher: `/home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os/bin/decision-os-server.mjs`.
- Run it from the target workspace cwd so `.decision-os/state.json` resolves correctly.
- Use `setsid sh -c 'cd <workspace> && exec env PORT=<port> <launcher> >> <log> 2>&1' </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &`
  for a real background server.
- Redirect stdout and stderr to a workspace-specific log under `/tmp`.
- Verify with `curl -I` before reporting the URL.
- Do not rely on a plain foreground command for operator-facing server sessions.
- Do not rely on a fragile one-liner that only backgrounds the wrapper without verifying the child server stayed alive.

## Launcher Notes

The launcher derives decision-os runtime paths from its own location and sets:

```bash
DECISION_OS_FRONTEND_ROOT=/home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os/frontend
TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=/home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os/backend/tsconfig.json
```

To inspect the underlying command without starting the server:

```bash
/home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os/bin/decision-os-server.mjs --print-command
````

````text
---
name: task-group-completeness
description: Audit proposed task groups for missing work, verification gaps, forgotten files, uncovered scenarios, absent migrations, fixture gaps, config gaps, and unresolved handoff data. Repair the injected input card when evidence supports changes, then write the injected report card. Use after task-dependency and before implementation-orchestrator launches workers.
---

## A. Purpose

1. This skill audits proposed task groups before dispatch to implementation workers.
2. It prevents workers from rediscovering missing tasks, missing verification, forgotten files, uncovered scenarios, absent migrations, fixture gaps, config gaps, and handoff gaps.
3. It returns `ready` only when the groups are complete enough for dispatch, and `blocked` when unresolved questions prevent dispatch.

---

## B. Audit

1. Build a coverage matrix across requirements, scenarios, target files, tests, migrations, fixtures, config, and handoff data.
2. Check that every source requirement maps to at least one task.
3. Check that every task maps to one proposed group.
4. Check that every behavior-changing task has verification coverage through tests, scenario checks, inspections, and documented verification reasons.
5. Treat missing verification as a blocking gap unless source evidence proves verification cannot be supplied.

---

## C. Input Card Changes

1. Repair the injected **input card** before writing the report card when evidence supports a concrete change.
2. Add missing implementation tasks, verification tasks, migration tasks, fixture tasks, config tasks, file targets, scenario coverage, dependency notes, and handoff data directly to the input card.
3. Amend existing tasks in the input card when the target file, dependency, test, scenario, migration, fixture, config, acceptance condition, and handoff detail are incomplete.
4. Leave a blocking question instead of editing only when source evidence does not determine the correct card change.
5. Keep the edited card in the same structure and style as this skill.

---

## D. Report Card

1. Write the audit report into the injected **report card** after the input card changes are complete.
2. The report card records what was checked, what was changed in the input card, which groups are approved, which gaps remain, and the final dispatch decision.
3. Include `Group Completeness Matrix`, `Input Card Edits Applied`, `Approved Groups`, `Required Additions`, `Blocking Questions`, and `Dispatch Readiness`.
4. Include group ids, task ids, source card ids, target files, verification tasks, migration tasks, fixture tasks, config tasks, unanswered questions, and final status using `ready` and `blocked`.
5. Keep the report card in the same structure and style as this skill.

---

## E. Hard Rules

1. Do not approve a group without checking requirements, files, tests, migrations, fixtures, config, handoff data, and scenarios.
2. Do not invent tasks without source evidence.
3. Do not leave an input-card correction only in the report card.
4. Use bold only for **important words** inside a sentence; do not turn each numbered item opening into a subtitle.
5. Do not implement product code and do not run implementation tests.
6. Do not change card status during this audit.
````

````text
---
name: task-group-completeness
description: Audit proposed task groups for missing work, verification gaps, forgotten files, uncovered scenarios, absent migrations, fixture gaps, config gaps, and unresolved handoff data. Repair the injected input card when evidence supports changes, then write the injected report card. Use after task-dependency and before implementation-orchestrator launches workers.
---

## A. Purpose

1. This skill audits **proposed task groups** before **implementation worker dispatch**.
2. It prevents workers from rediscovering **missing tasks**, **missing verification**, **forgotten files**, **uncovered scenarios**, **absent migrations**, **fixture gaps**, **config gaps**, and **handoff gaps**.
3. It returns `ready` only when the groups are **complete enough for dispatch**, and `blocked` when **unresolved questions** prevent dispatch.

---

## B. Audit

1. Build a **coverage matrix** across **requirements**, **scenarios**, **target files**, **tests**, **migrations**, **fixtures**, **config**, and **handoff data**.
2. Check that every **source requirement** maps to at least one **task**.
3. Check that every **task** maps to one **proposed group**.
4. Check that every **behavior-changing task** has **verification coverage** through **tests**, **scenario checks**, **inspections**, and **documented verification reasons**.
5. Treat **missing verification** as a **blocking gap** unless **source evidence** proves verification cannot be supplied.

---

## C. Input Card Changes

1. Repair the injected **input card** before writing the **report card** when evidence supports a **concrete change**.
2. Add **missing implementation tasks**, **verification tasks**, **migration tasks**, **fixture tasks**, **config tasks**, **file targets**, **scenario coverage**, **dependency notes**, and **handoff data** directly to the input card.
3. Amend **existing tasks** in the input card when the **target file**, **dependency**, **test**, **scenario**, **migration**, **fixture**, **config**, **acceptance condition**, and **handoff detail** are incomplete.
4. Leave a **blocking question** instead of editing only when **source evidence** does not determine the **correct card change**.
5. Keep the edited card in the **same structure and style** as this skill.

---

## D. Report Card

1. Write the **audit report** into the injected **report card** after the **input card changes** are complete.
2. The report card records what was **checked**, what was **changed in the input card**, which groups are **approved**, which gaps **remain**, and the final **dispatch decision**.
3. Include the **report sections** `Group Completeness Matrix`, `Input Card Edits Applied`, `Approved Groups`, `Required Additions`, `Blocking Questions`, and `Dispatch Readiness`.
4. Include **group ids**, **task ids**, **source card ids**, **target files**, **verification tasks**, **migration tasks**, **fixture tasks**, **config tasks**, **unanswered questions**, and final status using `ready` and `blocked`.
5. Keep the report card in the **same structure and style** as this skill.

---

## E. Hard Rules

1. Do not approve a **group** without checking **requirements**, **files**, **tests**, **migrations**, **fixtures**, **config**, **handoff data**, and **scenarios**.
2. Do not invent **tasks** without **source evidence**.
3. Do not leave an **input-card correction** only in the **report card**.
4. Use bold only for the **important words that carry the point** inside a sentence; do not turn each **numbered item opening** into a subtitle.
5. Do not implement **product code** and do not run **implementation tests**.
6. Do not change **card status** during this audit.
````

````text
---
name: decision-os-treat-open-notes
description: Use when the user says "treat open notes", "treat open notes in <ledger>", "answer open notes", "process unanswered notes", or asks to handle unanswered decision-os threads. Query the ledger in the agent cwd by default, answer pending operator notes, and verify no unanswered notes remain.
---

# decision-os Treat Open Notes

## A. Formatting Contract

1. **Headings:** use `H2` card sections with uppercase letters: `## A. Scope`, `## B. Contract`, `## C. Acceptance Criteria`.
2. **Dividers:** put `---` between card sections.
3. **Lists:** write section content as numbered list items: `1.`, `2.`, `3.`.
4. **Bold:** use **bold** for the important words that carry the point.
5. **Backticks:** use `backticks` for technical, secondary, exact, or literal terms: file paths, routes, config keys, commands, IDs, statuses, branch names, code symbols, and literal values.

## Purpose

Treat decision-os notes as the operator-to-agent inbox. Find unanswered operator notes in the current workspace ledger, do the requested work, persist the agent answer, and verify completion.

## Default Target

Use the agent shell cwd as the target workspace by default. Look for `.decision-os/` in that cwd first. Do not jump to any other directory unless the user explicitly names it.

If the user names a workspace, ledger, route, tab, or article, use that explicit target. Otherwise, resolve ledgers from the cwd workspace.

Resolve the decision-os runtime repo before using the ledger CLI:

```bash
if [ -n "${DECISION_OS_REPO:-}" ]; then
  DECISION_OS_REPO="$DECISION_OS_REPO"
elif [ -x "bin/ledger-cli.mjs" ]; then
  DECISION_OS_REPO="$(pwd)"
elif git rev-parse --show-toplevel >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -x "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/bin/ledger-cli.mjs" ]; then
  DECISION_OS_REPO="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
else
  printf 'Unable to resolve decision-os repo. Set DECISION_OS_REPO or run from a decision-os checkout.\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi
LEDGER_CLI="$DECISION_OS_REPO/bin/ledger-cli.mjs"
```

To inspect the available command syntax:

```bash
node "$LEDGER_CLI" help
```

Use the help output for CLI syntax. Keep treatment policy, Markdown patching rules, and safety rules from this skill as the source of truth for how to answer notes.

## Resolve Ledgers

Start from:

```bash
pwd
find .decision-os -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.json' -print
```

Prefer `.decision-os/state.json` for active tabs/routes when it exists. If the user names a ledger, match the name against state entries and `.decision-os/*.json` filenames. If no ledger is named, query the active/default ledger from state; if state is ambiguous, query all non-state ledger JSON files under `.decision-os/`.

## Query Open Notes

Use the decision-os ledger CLI launcher from the target workspace cwd:

```bash
node "$LEDGER_CLI" unanswered --ledger <ledger-json> --json
```

For human-readable output:

```bash
node "$LEDGER_CLI" unanswered --ledger <ledger-json>
```

The output provides `threadId`, `threadFile`, pending messages, and a suggested answer command. Read the full `threadFile` before answering. Also read the related card content under `.decision-os/cards/...` when the note refers to card content, design state, implementation details, or requested edits.

## Markdown Content Files Are The Primary Edit Surface

Most card bodies and thread histories are stored in Markdown content files under `.decision-os/cards/...` and `.decision-os/threads/...`. In most cases, updating the relevant Markdown file is enough.

Do not manually update ledger JSON when the requested change is only card prose, requirements text, notes, or an agent reply. Ledger JSON should only be edited when changing structured ledger data such as card geometry, titles, labels, relationships, zones, status, or explicit schema fields.

For thread answers, patch the `threadFile` directly for structured Markdown replies, or use `ledger-cli answer` for short plain-text replies. Do not regenerate ledger JSON manually for a thread reply.

## Treat Each Note

For every pending operator note:

1. Understand the request from the note, thread history, target card/zone title, and relevant card content.
2. Perform the requested repo or ledger work before replying when the note asks for a change.
3. Update durable card content in the card content file when the operator requested a design/content change; the thread reply confirms the work, but the card file is the persistent state.
4. Write a concrete answer that closes the request or states the blocker and exact next step.

Avoid generic acknowledgements. Answer the substance of the note.

Never change a card status while treating open notes unless the operator explicitly asks for a status change. Do not mark cards `done`, `todo`, processing, or similar as a side effect of answering a note.

## Durable Card Formatting

When creating or rewriting decision-os card content, use this formatting by default unless the operator explicitly asks for a different format:

1. Use only `H2` section headings for card sections.
2. Prefix every `H2` section heading with an explicit uppercase section letter and period, for example `## A. Scope`, `## B. Server Contract`, `## C. Client Contract`.
3. Put `---` horizontal rules between sections.
4. Use numbered lists for section content; do not use unordered bullet lists for normal card requirements.
5. Use **bold** for important labels or concepts at the start of each numbered item.
6. Use `backticks` for file paths, config keys, API routes, method codes, literal values, statuses, and other exact tokens.
7. Keep card prose concrete and implementation-ready. Avoid generic acknowledgements inside durable card content.
8. When splitting one note into multiple cards, apply this formatting to every created or edited card.

## Persist Answers

For short plain-text answers, the CLI is acceptable:

```bash
node "$LEDGER_CLI" answer --ledger <ledger-json> --thread-id <thread-id> --message "..."
```

For multi-paragraph answers, markdown tables, code, bullets, or structured content, patch the `threadFile` directly instead of passing content through `--message`. Append exactly one agent section:

```markdown
# AGENT
<!-- decision-os:note {"id":"note-agent-<epoch-ms>-<8-hex>","timestamp":"<ISO-8601>"} -->

Answer markdown here.
```

Use only `# OPERATOR` and `# AGENT` as top-level message headings. Generate a unique note id and current ISO-8601 timestamp. Do not regenerate or hand-edit ledger JSON for a thread reply.

## Verify

After answering, rerun:

```bash
node "$LEDGER_CLI" unanswered --ledger <ledger-json>
```

Treat the work as complete only when the relevant ledgers report no unanswered notes, or when remaining notes are explicitly blocked. Report the ledgers checked, thread ids answered, files changed, and any remaining open threads.
````

````text
---
name: task-group-completeness
description: Audit proposed task groups for missing work, verification gaps, forgotten files, uncovered scenarios, absent migrations, fixture gaps, config gaps, and unresolved handoff data. Repair the injected input card when evidence supports changes, then write the injected report card. Use after task-dependency and before implementation-orchestrator launches workers.
---

## A. Purpose

1. This skill audits **proposed task groups** before **implementation worker dispatch**.
2. It prevents workers from rediscovering **missing tasks**, **missing verification**, **forgotten files**, **uncovered scenarios**, **absent migrations**, **fixture gaps**, **config gaps**, and **handoff gaps**.
3. It returns `ready` only when the groups are **complete enough for dispatch**, and `blocked` when **unresolved questions** prevent dispatch.

---

## B. Audit

1. Build a **coverage matrix** across **requirements**, **scenarios**, **target files**, **tests**, **migrations**, **fixtures**, **config**, and **handoff data**.
2. Check that every **source requirement** maps to at least one **task**.
3. Check that every **task** maps to one **proposed group**.
4. Check that every **behavior-changing task** has **verification coverage** through **tests**, **scenario checks**, **inspections**, and **documented verification reasons**.
5. Treat **missing verification** as a **blocking gap** unless **source evidence** proves verification cannot be supplied.

---

## C. Input Card Changes

1. Repair the injected **input card** before writing the **report card** when evidence supports a **concrete change**.
2. Add **missing implementation tasks**, **verification tasks**, **migration tasks**, **fixture tasks**, **config tasks**, **file targets**, **scenario coverage**, **dependency notes**, and **handoff data** directly to the input card.
3. Amend **existing tasks** in the input card when the **target file**, **dependency**, **test**, **scenario**, **migration**, **fixture**, **config**, **acceptance condition**, and **handoff detail** are incomplete.
4. Leave a **blocking question** instead of editing only when **source evidence** does not determine the **correct card change**.
5. Keep the edited card in the **same structure and style** as this skill.

---

## D. Report Card

1. Write the **audit report** into the injected **report card** after the **input card changes** are complete.
2. The report card records what was **checked**, what was **changed in the input card**, which groups are **approved**, which gaps **remain**, and the final **dispatch decision**.
3. Include the **report sections** `Group Completeness Matrix`, `Input Card Edits Applied`, `Approved Groups`, `Required Additions`, `Blocking Questions`, and `Dispatch Readiness`.
4. Include **group ids**, **task ids**, **source card ids**, **target files**, **verification tasks**, **migration tasks**, **fixture tasks**, **config tasks**, **unanswered questions**, and final status using `ready` and `blocked`.
5. Keep the report card in the **same structure and style** as this skill.

---

## E. Hard Rules

1. Do not approve a **group** without checking **requirements**, **files**, **tests**, **migrations**, **fixtures**, **config**, **handoff data**, and **scenarios**.
2. Do not invent **tasks** without **source evidence**.
3. Do not leave an **input-card correction** only in the **report card**.
4. Use bold only for the **important words that carry the point** inside a sentence; do not turn each **numbered item opening** into a subtitle.
5. Do not implement **product code** and do not run **implementation tests**.
6. Do not change **card status** during this audit.
````

`````text
find .decision-os -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.json' -print

Prefer `.decision-os/state.json` for active tabs/routes when it exists. If the user names a ledger, match the name against state entries and `.decision-os/*.json` filenames. If no ledger is named, query the active/default ledger from state; if state is ambiguous, query all non-state ledger JSON files under `.decision-os/`.

## Query Open Notes

Use the decision-os ledger CLI launcher from the target workspace cwd:

```bash
node "$LEDGER_CLI" unanswered --ledger <ledger-json> --json
```

For human-readable output:

```bash
node "$LEDGER_CLI" unanswered --ledger <ledger-json>
```

The output provides `threadId`, `threadFile`, pending messages, and a suggested answer command. Read the full `threadFile` before answering. Also read the related card content under `.decision-os/cards/...` when the note refers to card content, design state, implementation details, or requested edits.

## Markdown Content Files Are The Primary Edit Surface

Most card bodies and thread histories are stored in Markdown content files under `.decision-os/cards/...` and `.decision-os/threads/...`. In most cases, updating the relevant Markdown file is enough.

Do not manually update ledger JSON when the requested change is only card prose, requirements text, notes, or an agent reply. Ledger JSON should only be edited when changing structured ledger data such as card geometry, titles, labels, relationships, zones, status, or explicit schema fields.

For thread answers, patch the `threadFile` directly for structured Markdown replies, or use `ledger-cli answer` for short plain-text replies. Do not regenerate ledger JSON manually for a thread reply.

## Treat Each Note

For every pending operator note:

1. Understand the request from the note, thread history, target card/zone title, and relevant card content.
2. Perform the requested repo or ledger work before replying when the note asks for a change.
3. Update durable card content in the card content file when the operator requested a design/content change; the thread reply confirms the work, but the card file is the persistent state.
4. Write a concrete answer that closes the request or states the blocker and exact next step.

Avoid generic acknowledgements. Answer the substance of the note.

Never change a card status while treating open notes unless the operator explicitly asks for a status change. Do not mark cards `done`, `todo`, processing, or similar as a side effect of answering a note.

## Durable Card Formatting

When creating or rewriting decision-os card content, use this formatting by default unless the operator explicitly asks for a different format:

1. Use only `H2` section headings for card sections.
2. Prefix every `H2` section heading with an explicit uppercase section letter and period, for example `## A. Scope`, `## B. Server Contract`, `## C. Client Contract`.
3. Put `---` horizontal rules between sections.
4. Use numbered lists for section content; do not use unordered bullet lists for normal card requirements.
5. Use **bold** for important labels or concepts at the start of each numbered item.
6. Use `backticks` for file paths, config keys, API routes, method codes, literal values, statuses, and other exact tokens.
7. Keep card prose concrete and implementation-ready. Avoid generic acknowledgements inside durable card content.
8. When splitting one note into multiple cards, apply this formatting to every created or edited card.

## Persist Answers

For short plain-text answers, the CLI is acceptable:

```bash
node "$LEDGER_CLI" answer --ledger <ledger-json> --thread-id <thread-id> --message "..."
```

For multi-paragraph answers, markdown tables, code, bullets, or structured content, patch the `threadFile` directly instead of passing content through `--message`. Append exactly one agent section:

```markdown
# AGENT
<!-- decision-os:note {"id":"note-agent-<epoch-ms>-<8-hex>","timestamp":"<ISO-8601>"} -->

Answer markdown here.
```

Use only `# OPERATOR` and `# AGENT` as top-level message headings. Generate a unique note id and current ISO-8601 timestamp. Do not regenerate or hand-edit ledger JSON for a thread reply.

## Verify

After answering, rerun:

```bash
node "$LEDGER_CLI" unanswered --ledger <ledger-json>
```

Treat the work as complete only when the relevant ledgers report no unanswered notes, or when remaining notes are explicitly blocked. Report the ledgers checked, thread ids answered, files changed, and any remaining open threads.
`````

````text
---
````
````text
name: task-group-completeness
description: Perform a deep engineering completeness review of proposed task groups against the full stack, complete specs, data model, runtime state, and operator constraints. Repair the injected input card when fundamental tasks are missing, then write the injected report card. Use after task-dependency and before implementation-orchestrator launches workers.
---

## A. Purpose

1. This skill performs a **deep engineering completeness review** of **proposed task groups** before **implementation worker dispatch**.
2. It judges whether the plan is **logically solid**, **technically complete**, and grounded in the **full stack**, **complete specs**, **data model**, **runtime state**, and **operator constraints**.
3. It returns `ready` only when no **fundamental implementation tasks** are missing, and `blocked` when **planning logic** has unresolved gaps.

---

## B. Deep Planning Audit

1. Reconstruct the **implementation logic** from the injected source material, not just the **task list**.
2. Judge whether the grouped plan would produce a **coherent implementation** across **architecture**, **data**, **state**, **APIs**, **UI**, **config**, **migrations**, **tests**, **fixtures**, and **handoff**.
3. Look for **fundamental missing tasks** that would make implementation fail even when every requirement appears mapped and every task appears grouped.
4. Treat traceability checks as **supporting evidence**, not the **audit result**.
5. Reject a plan that is only **performatively complete**: named tasks, mapped requirements, and grouped work are not enough to prove **engineering completeness**.

---

## C. Input Card Changes

1. Repair the injected **input card** before writing the **report card** when deep analysis finds a **fundamental task gap**.
2. Add missing tasks needed for **architecture boundaries**, **data model changes**, **state transitions**, **API contracts**, **UI behavior**, **config changes**, **migrations**, **fixtures**, **test strategy**, and **handoff data**.
3. Amend **existing groups** when they hide **dependencies**, **sequencing risks**, **shared-file collisions**, **missing integration work**, **missing verification strategy**, and **unclear implementation ownership**.
4. Leave a **blocking question** only when the full stack and spec evidence does not determine the **necessary task**.
5. Keep the edited card in the **same structure and style** as this skill.

---

## D. Report Card

1. Write the **audit report** into the injected **report card** after the **input card changes** are complete.
2. The report card explains the **engineering reasoning**, the **planning risks tested**, the **input card repairs**, the **remaining gaps**, and the final **dispatch decision**.
3. Include the **report sections** `Engineering Completeness Findings`, `Fundamental Missing Tasks`, `Input Card Edits Applied`, `Dispatch-Ready Groups`, `Blocking Questions`, and `Dispatch Readiness`.
4. Include **group ids**, **task ids**, **source card ids**, **target files**, **missing engineering logic**, **verification strategy**, **migration needs**, **fixture needs**, **config needs**, **unanswered questions**, and final status using `ready` and `blocked`.
5. Keep the report card in the **same structure and style** as this skill.

---

## E. Hard Rules

1. Do not approve a **group** from **checkbox traceability** without testing the **engineering logic** behind the plan.
2. Do not invent **tasks** without **source evidence**.
3. Do not treat **requirement-to-task mapping** and **task-to-group mapping** as proof of **planning completeness**.
4. Do not leave an **input-card correction** only in the **report card**.
5. Use bold only for the **important words that carry the point** inside a sentence; do not turn each **numbered item opening** into a subtitle.
6. Do not implement **product code** and do not run **implementation tests**.
7. Do not change **card status** during this audit.
````

---
````text
name: task-group-completeness
description: Perform a deep engineering completeness review of proposed task groups against the full stack, complete specs, data model, runtime state, and operator constraints. Repair the injected input card when fundamental tasks are missing, then write the injected report card. Use after task-dependency and before implementation-orchestrator launches workers.
---

## A. Purpose

1. This skill performs a **deep engineering completeness review** of **proposed task groups** before **implementation worker dispatch**.
2. It judges whether the plan is **logically solid**, **technically complete**, and grounded in the **full stack**, **complete specs**, **data model**, **runtime state**, and **operator constraints**.
3. It returns `ready` only when no **fundamental implementation tasks** are missing, and `blocked` when **planning logic** has unresolved gaps.

---

## B. Deep Planning Audit

1. Reconstruct the **implementation logic** from the injected source material, not just the **task list**.
2. Judge whether the grouped plan would produce a **coherent implementation** across **architecture**, **data**, **state**, **APIs**, **UI**, **config**, **migrations**, **tests**, **fixtures**, and **handoff**.
3. Look for **fundamental missing tasks** that would make implementation fail even when every requirement appears mapped and every task appears grouped.
4. Treat traceability checks as **supporting evidence**, not the **audit result**.
5. Reject a plan that is only **performatively complete**: named tasks, mapped requirements, and grouped work are not enough to prove **engineering completeness**.

---

## C. Input Card Changes

1. Repair the injected **input card** before writing the **report card** when deep analysis finds a **fundamental task gap**.
2. Add missing tasks needed for **architecture boundaries**, **data model changes**, **state transitions**, **API contracts**, **UI behavior**, **config changes**, **migrations**, **fixtures**, **test strategy**, and **handoff data**.
3. Amend **existing groups** when they hide **dependencies**, **sequencing risks**, **shared-file collisions**, **missing integration work**, **missing verification strategy**, and **unclear implementation ownership**.
4. Leave a **blocking question** only when the full stack and spec evidence does not determine the **necessary task**.
5. Keep the edited card in the **same structure and style** as this skill.

---

## D. Report Card

1. Write the **audit report** into the injected **report card** after the **input card changes** are complete.
2. The report card explains the **engineering reasoning**, the **planning risks tested**, the **input card repairs**, the **remaining gaps**, and the final **dispatch decision**.
3. Include the **report sections** `Engineering Completeness Findings`, `Fundamental Missing Tasks`, `Input Card Edits Applied`, `Dispatch-Ready Groups`, `Blocking Questions`, and `Dispatch Readiness`.
4. Include **group ids**, **task ids**, **source card ids**, **target files**, **missing engineering logic**, **verification strategy**, **migration needs**, **fixture needs**, **config needs**, **unanswered questions**, and final status using `ready` and `blocked`.
5. Keep the report card in the **same structure and style** as this skill.

---

## E. Hard Rules

1. Do not approve a **group** from **checkbox traceability** without testing the **engineering logic** behind the plan.
2. Do not invent **tasks** without **source evidence**.
3. Do not treat **requirement-to-task mapping** and **task-to-group mapping** as proof of **planning completeness**.
4. Do not leave an **input-card correction** only in the **report card**.
5. Use bold only for the **important words that carry the point** inside a sentence; do not turn each **numbered item opening** into a subtitle.
6. Do not implement **product code** and do not run **implementation tests**.
7. Do not change **card status** during this audit.
````
