Requirement\n\n- Do not end a turn with a dirty `git status`.\n- By the end of the turn, the repository must be clean.\n- If code changed, you must end the turn with a proper git commit unless the operator explicitly says not to commit.\n- If documentation or design/spec artifacts changed as part of the requested work, those changes must also be committed before ending the turn unless the operator explicitly says not to commit.\n- A proper commit means:\n  - the commit message reflects the real intent of the staged diff\n  - the staged diff matches a coherent unit of work\n  - relevant verification has been run when feasible before commit\n- Do not treat leftover changes as safely \"unrelated\" by default. Assume they may be unfinished work from a prior turn.\n- If the tree is already dirty, you must perform a reconciliation step before committing:\n  - inspect the existing changes\n  - analyze their intent\n  - decide whether they belong in the current unit of work or a separate one\n  - ensure the final commit structure respects that intent\n- If reconciliation reveals multiple intents, use separate commits rather than one mixed commit unless the operator explicitly requests otherwise.\n- Do not end a code-changing turn with uncommitted changes without explicitly stating why that was unavoidable.\n\n\n## JavaScript REPL (Node)\n- Use `js_repl` for Node-backed JavaScript with top-level await in a persistent kernel.\n- `js_repl` is a freeform/custom tool. Direct `js_repl` calls must send raw JavaScript tool input (optionally with first-line `// codex-js-repl: timeout_ms=15000`). Do not wrap code in JSON (for example `{\"code\":\"...\"}`), quotes, or markdown code fences.\n- Helpers: `codex.tmpDir`, `codex.tool(name, args?)`, and `codex.emitImage(imageLike)`.\n- `codex.tool` executes a normal tool call and resolves to the raw tool output object. Use it for shell and non-shell tools alike. Nested tool outputs stay inside JavaScript unless you emit them explicitly.\n- `codex.emitImage(...)` adds one image to the outer `js_repl` function output each time you call it, so you can call it multiple times to emit multiple images. It accepts a data URL, a single `input_image` item, an object like `{ bytes, mimeType }`, or a raw tool response object with exactly one image and no text. It rejects mixed text-and-image content.\n- Example of sharing an in-memory Playwright screenshot: `await codex.emitImage({ bytes: await page.screenshot({ type: \"jpeg\", quality: 85 }), mimeType: \"image/jpeg\" })`.\n- Example of sharing a local image tool result: `await codex.emitImage(codex.tool(\"view_image\", { path: \"/absolute/path\" }))`.\n- When encoding an image to send with `codex.emitImage(...)` or `view_image`, prefer JPEG at about 85 quality when lossy compression is acceptable; use PNG when transparency or lossless detail matters. Smaller uploads are faster and less likely to hit size limits.\n- Top-level bindings persist across cells. If a cell throws, prior bindings remain available and bindings that finished initializing before the throw often remain usable in later cells. For code you plan to reuse across cells, prefer declaring or assigning it in direct top-level statements before operations that might throw. If you hit `SyntaxError: Identifier 'x' has already been declared`, first reuse the existing binding, reassign a previously declared `let`, or pick a new descriptive name. Use `{ ... }` only for a short temporary block when you specifically need local scratch names; do not wrap an entire cell in block scope if you want those names reusable later. Reset the kernel with `js_repl_reset` only when you need a clean state.\n- Top-level static import declarations (for example `import x from \"./file.js\"`) are currently unsupported in `js_repl`; use dynamic imports with `await import(\"pkg\")`, `await import(\"./file.js\")`, or `await import(\"/abs/path/file.mjs\")` instead. Imported local files must be ESM `.js`/`.mjs` files and run in the same REPL VM context. Bare package imports always resolve from REPL-global search roots (`CODEX_JS_REPL_NODE_MODULE_DIRS`, then cwd), not relative to the imported file location. Local files may statically import only other local relative/absolute/`file://` `.js`/`.mjs` files; package and builtin imports from local files must stay dynamic. `import.meta.resolve()` returns importable strings such as `file://...`, bare package names, and `node:...` specifiers. Local file modules reload between execs, while top-level bindings persist until `js_repl_reset`.\n- Avoid direct access to `process.stdout` / `process.stderr` / `process.stdin`; it can corrupt the JSON line protocol. Use `console.log`, `codex.tool(...)`, and `codex.emitImage(...)`.\n\n## Skills\nA skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. (file: /home/jbb/.codex/skills/positioning-canvas/SKILL.md)\n- strategic-narrative: Use when asked to \"strategic narrative\", \"Andy Raskin\", \"tell our company story\", \"write a pitch deck\", \"explain why customers should care\", or \"movement narrative\". 7605:/home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os/.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-c48369dc-1d97-4c6c-ab36-fd01d819d03a.md:1563:.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4:Ici, on a besoin de créer un skill qui va prendre le résultat du skill qu'on avait créé qui s'appelle Screen Content Planner, corrigé d'une bloat analysis éventuellement. En tout cas, ça prend une description de skill et enfin, ça prend une description de screen, pardon, et ça les transforme en mock-up visuel. Ce que ça fait, c'est que si jamais c'est une technologie web, on les fait directement, en fait, quoi qu'il arrive, en fait, on les fait en HTML et CSS. Et il faut bien que le skill, avant de générer les screens, il fasse une analyse complète des styles avec les couleurs, les border radius. En fait, il faut réutiliser ce qu'il y a dans Frontend skill pour pouvoir faire une analyse du design qu'on a dans l'application pour que les mock-ups, ils soient cohérents avec ce qu'on a déjà dans l'application. Et ensuite, ce qu'il faut que ça fasse, c'est que ça, du coup, ça génère les fichiers HTML et CSS, le CSS séparé du HTML à chaque fois. Chaque screen, il est dans son fichier HTML et chaque fichier HTML, il a son fichier CSS. Et ensuite, ce qu'on fait, c'est qu'on render avec le format d'image correct qui correspond à ce qu'on est en train de faire. Donc, par exemple, si c'est une application mobile en mode portrait, il faut qu'on fasse un render dans du browser en 9 16e et qu'on fasse ensuite une capture d'image et qu'on construise un carrousel dans la carte pour pouvoir montrer tous les mock-ups dans un carrousel. C'est aussi important que dans le skill, il y ait les règles de formatting qu'on a pour décision OS. Et ça veut dire qu'à chaque fois, je veux que les outputs soient créés avec les règles de formatting. Donc, ça veut dire que nos règles de formatting, il faut qu'on les ajoute à chaque skill qui est une tâche que tu dois faire alternative. Non, non, oublie cette tâche, je veux la faire moi-même. En tout cas, dans le skill que tu crées, il faudra mettre les règles de formatting et les règles de formatting, du coup, c'est les règles de formatting des cartes. C'est-à-dire que quand output du markdown, il faut que les titres, ils aient une lettre, que les sous-titres, ils aient une lettre un numéro, que les bullet points, elles aient des numéros, il faut que chaque section, elle soit séparée par un HR et il faut qu'il y ait du bold et des bactics.

Requirement\n\n- Do not end a turn with a dirty `git status`.\n- By the end of the turn, the repository must be clean.\n- If code changed, you must end the turn with a proper git commit unless the operator explicitly says not to commit.\n- If documentation or design/spec artifacts changed as part of the requested work, those changes must also be committed before ending the turn unless the operator explicitly says not to commit.\n- A proper commit means:\n  - the commit message reflects the real intent of the staged diff\n  - the staged diff matches a coherent unit of work\n  - relevant verification has been run when feasible before commit\n- Do not treat leftover changes as safely \"unrelated\" by default. Assume they may be unfinished work from a prior turn.\n- If the tree is already dirty, you must perform a reconciliation step before committing:\n  - inspect the existing changes\n  - analyze their intent\n  - decide whether they belong in the current unit of work or a separate one\n  - ensure the final commit structure respects that intent\n- If reconciliation reveals multiple intents, use separate commits rather than one mixed commit unless the operator explicitly requests otherwise.\n- Do not end a code-changing turn with uncommitted changes without explicitly stating why that was unavoidable.\n\n\n## JavaScript REPL (Node)\n- Use `js_repl` for Node-backed JavaScript with top-level await in a persistent kernel.\n- `js_repl` is a freeform/custom tool. Direct `js_repl` calls must send raw JavaScript tool input (optionally with first-line `// codex-js-repl: timeout_ms=15000`). Do not wrap code in JSON (for example `{\"code\":\"...\"}`), quotes, or markdown code fences.\n- Helpers: `codex.tmpDir`, `codex.tool(name, args?)`, and `codex.emitImage(imageLike)`.\n- `codex.tool` executes a normal tool call and resolves to the raw tool output object. Use it for shell and non-shell tools alike. Nested tool outputs stay inside JavaScript unless you emit them explicitly.\n- `codex.emitImage(...)` adds one image to the outer `js_repl` function output each time you call it, so you can call it multiple times to emit multiple images. It accepts a data URL, a single `input_image` item, an object like `{ bytes, mimeType }`, or a raw tool response object with exactly one image and no text. It rejects mixed text-and-image content.\n- Example of sharing an in-memory Playwright screenshot: `await codex.emitImage({ bytes: await page.screenshot({ type: \"jpeg\", quality: 85 }), mimeType: \"image/jpeg\" })`.\n- Example of sharing a local image tool result: `await codex.emitImage(codex.tool(\"view_image\", { path: \"/absolute/path\" }))`.\n- When encoding an image to send with `codex.emitImage(...)` or `view_image`, prefer JPEG at about 85 quality when lossy compression is acceptable; use PNG when transparency or lossless detail matters. Smaller uploads are faster and less likely to hit size limits.\n- Top-level bindings persist across cells. If a cell throws, prior bindings remain available and bindings that finished initializing before the throw often remain usable in later cells. For code you plan to reuse across cells, prefer declaring or assigning it in direct top-level statements before operations that might throw. If you hit `SyntaxError: Identifier 'x' has already been declared`, first reuse the existing binding, reassign a previously declared `let`, or pick a new descriptive name. Use `{ ... }` only for a short temporary block when you specifically need local scratch names; do not wrap an entire cell in block scope if you want those names reusable later. Reset the kernel with `js_repl_reset` only when you need a clean state.\n- Top-level static import declarations (for example `import x from \"./file.js\"`) are currently unsupported in `js_repl`; use dynamic imports with `await import(\"pkg\")`, `await import(\"./file.js\")`, or `await import(\"/abs/path/file.mjs\")` instead. Imported local files must be ESM `.js`/`.mjs` files and run in the same REPL VM context. Bare package imports always resolve from REPL-global search roots (`CODEX_JS_REPL_NODE_MODULE_DIRS`, then cwd), not relative to the imported file location. Local files may statically import only other local relative/absolute/`file://` `.js`/`.mjs` files; package and builtin imports from local files must stay dynamic. `import.meta.resolve()` returns importable strings such as `file://...`, bare package names, and `node:...` specifiers. Local file modules reload between execs, while top-level bindings persist until `js_repl_reset`.\n- Avoid direct access to `process.stdout` / `process.stderr` / `process.stdin`; it can corrupt the JSON line protocol. Use `console.log`, `codex.tool(...)`, and `codex.emitImage(...)`.\n\n## Skills\nA skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. This skill should be used when users want to create a new skill (or update an existing skill) that extends Codex's capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, or tool integrations.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:750:  short-description: Create or update a skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:755:This skill provides guidance for creating effective skills.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:795:You may use subagents during iteration to validate whether a skill works on realistic tasks or whether a suspected problem is real. This is most useful when you want an independent pass on the skill's behavior, outputs, or failure modes after a revision.  Only do this when it is possible to start new subagents.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:797:When using subagents for validation, treat that as an evaluation surface. The goal is to learn whether the skill generalizes, not whether another agent can reconstruct the answer from leaked context.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:803:Every skill consists of a required SKILL.md file and optional bundled resources:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:806:skill-name/\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:813:│   └── openai.yaml - UI metadata for skill lists and chips\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:824:- **Frontmatter** (YAML): Contains `name` and `description` fields. These are the only fields that Codex reads to determine when the skill gets used, thus it is very important to be clear and comprehensive in describing what the skill is, and when it should be used.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:825:- **Body** (Markdown): Instructions and guidance for using the skill. Only loaded AFTER the skill triggers (if at all).\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:829:- UI-facing metadata for skill lists and chips\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:831:- Create: human-facing `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt` by reading the skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:832:- Generate deterministically by passing the values as `--interface key=value` to `scripts/generate_openai_yaml.py` or `scripts/init_skill.py`\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:857:- **Avoid duplication**: Information should live in either SKILL.md or references files, not both. Prefer references files for detailed information unless it's truly core to the skill—this keeps SKILL.md lean while making information discoverable without hogging the context window. Keep only essential procedural instructions and workflow guidance in SKILL.md; move detailed reference material, schemas, and examples to references files.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:863:- **When to include**: When the skill needs files that will be used in the final output\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:870:A skill should only contain essential files that directly support its functionality. Do NOT create extraneous documentation or auxiliary files, including:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:878:The skill should only contain the information needed for an AI agent to do the job at hand. It should not contain auxiliary context about the process that went into creating it, setup and testing procedures, user-facing documentation, etc. Creating additional documentation files just adds clutter and confusion.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:885:2. **SKILL.md body** - When skill triggers (<5k words)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:890:Keep SKILL.md body to the essentials and under 500 lines to minimize context bloat. Split content into separate files when approaching this limit. When splitting out content into other files, it is very important to reference them from SKILL.md and describe clearly when to read them, to ensure the reader of the skill knows they exist and when to use them.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:892:**Key principle:** When a skill supports multiple variations, frameworks, or options, keep only the core workflow and selection guidance in SKILL.md. Move variant-specific details (patterns, examples, configuration) into separate reference files.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:918:bigquery-skill/\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:929:Similarly, for skills supporting multiple frameworks or variants, organize by variant:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:972:1. Understand the skill with concrete examples\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:973:2. Plan reusable skill contents (scripts, references, assets)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:974:3. Initialize the skill (run init_skill.py)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:975:4. Edit the skill (implement resources and write SKILL.md)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:976:5. Validate the skill (run quick_validate.py)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:977:6. Iterate based on real usage and forward-test complex skills.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:987:- Name the skill folder exactly after the skill name.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:991:Skip this step only when the skill's usage patterns are already clearly understood. It remains valuable even when working with an existing skill.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:993:To create an effective skill, clearly understand concrete examples of how the skill will be used. This understanding can come from either direct user examples or generated examples that are validated with user feedback.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:995:For example, when building an image-editor skill, relevant questions include:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:997:- \"What functionality should the image-editor skill support? Editing, rotating, anything else?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:998:- \"Can you give some examples of how this skill would be used?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:999:- \"I can imagine users asking for things like 'Remove the red-eye from this image' or 'Rotate this image'. If they do not specify a location, default to `$CODEX_HOME/skills`; when `CODEX_HOME` is unset, fall back to `~/.codex/skills` so the skill is auto-discovered.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1141:When creating a new skill from scratch, always run the `init_skill.py` script. The script conveniently generates a new template skill directory that automatically includes everything a skill requires, making the skill creation process much more efficient and reliable.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1146:scripts/init_skill.py <skill-name> --path <output-directory> [--resources scripts,references,assets] [--examples]\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1152:scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path \"${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1153:scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path \"${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills\" --resources scripts,references\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1154:scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path ~/work/skills --resources scripts --examples\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1159:- Creates the skill directory at the specified path\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1167:Generate `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt` by reading the skill, then pass them as `--interface key=value` to `init_skill.py` or regenerate with:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1170:scripts/generate_openai_yaml.py <path/to/skill-folder> --interface key=value\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1177:When editing the (newly-generated or existing) skill, remember that the skill is being created for another instance of Codex to use. Include information that would be beneficial and non-obvious to Codex. Consider what procedural knowledge, domain-specific details, or reusable assets would help another Codex instance execute these tasks more effectively.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1179:After substantial revisions, or if the skill is particularly tricky, you should use subagents to forward-test the skill on realistic tasks or artifacts. When doing so, pass the artifact under validation rather than your diagnosis of what is wrong, and keep the prompt generic enough that success depends on transferable reasoning rather than hidden ground truth.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1183:To begin implementation, start with the reusable resources identified above: `scripts/`, `references/`, and `assets/` files. Note that this step may require user input. For example, when implementing a `brand-guidelines` skill, the user may need to provide brand assets or templates to store in `assets/`, or documentation to store in `references/`.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1187:If you used `--examples`, delete any placeholder files that are not needed for the skill. Only create resource directories that are actually required.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1197:- `name`: The skill name\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1198:- `description`: This is the primary triggering mechanism for your skill, and helps Codex understand when to use the skill.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1201:  - Example description for a `docx` skill: \"Comprehensive document creation, editing, and analysis with support for tracked changes, comments, formatting preservation, and text extraction. Only do this when it is possible to start new subagents.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2662:When using subagents for validation, treat that as an evaluation surface. The goal is to learn whether the skill generalizes, not whether another agent can reconstruct the answer from leaked context.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2668:Every skill consists of a required SKILL.md file and optional bundled resources:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2671:skill-name/\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2678:│   └── openai.yaml - UI metadata for skill lists and chips\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2689:- **Frontmatter** (YAML): Contains `name` and `description` fields. These are the only fields that Codex reads to determine when the skill gets used, thus it is very important to be clear and comprehensive in describing what the skill is, and when it should be used.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2690:- **Body** (Markdown): Instructions and guidance for using the skill. Only loaded AFTER the skill triggers (if at all).\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2694:- UI-facing metadata for skill lists and chips\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2696:- Create: human-facing `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt` by reading the skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2697:- Generate deterministically by passing the values as `--interface key=value` to `scripts/generate_openai_yaml.py` or `scripts/init_skill.py`\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2722:- **Avoid duplication**: Information should live in either SKILL.md or references files, not both. Prefer references files for detailed information unless it's truly core to the skill—this keeps SKILL.md lean while making information discoverable without hogging the context window. Keep only essential procedural instructions and workflow guidance in SKILL.md; move detailed reference material, schemas, and examples to references files.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2728:- **When to include**: When the skill needs files that will be used in the final output\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2735:A skill should only contain essential files that directly support its functionality. Do NOT create extraneous documentation or auxiliary files, including:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2743:The skill should only contain the information needed for an AI agent to do the job at hand. It should not contain auxiliary context about the process that went into creating it, setup and testing procedures, user-facing documentation, etc. Creating additional documentation files just adds clutter and confusion.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2750:2. **SKILL.md body** - When skill triggers (<5k words)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2755:Keep SKILL.md body to the essentials and under 500 lines to minimize context bloat. Split content into separate files when approaching this limit. When splitting out content into other files, it is very important to reference them from SKILL.md and describe clearly when to read them, to ensure the reader of the skill knows they exist and when to use them.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2757:**Key principle:** When a skill supports multiple variations, frameworks, or options, keep only the core workflow and selection guidance in SKILL.md. Move variant-specific details (patterns, examples, configuration) into separate reference files.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2783:bigquery-skill/\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2794:Similarly, for skills supporting multiple frameworks or variants, organize by variant:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2837:1. Understand the skill with concrete examples\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2838:2. Plan reusable skill contents (scripts, references, assets)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2839:3. Initialize the skill (run init_skill.py)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2840:4. Edit the skill (implement resources and write SKILL.md)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2841:5. Iterate based on real usage and forward-test complex skills.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2852:- Name the skill folder exactly after the skill name.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2856:Skip this step only when the skill's usage patterns are already clearly understood. It remains valuable even when working with an existing skill.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2858:To create an effective skill, clearly understand concrete examples of how the skill will be used. This understanding can come from either direct user examples or generated examples that are validated with user feedback.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2860:For example, when building an image-editor skill, relevant questions include:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2862:- \"What functionality should the image-editor skill support? Editing, rotating, anything else?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2863:- \"Can you give some examples of how this skill would be used?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2864:- \"I can imagine users asking for things like 'Remove the red-eye from this image' or 'Rotate this image'. Are there other ways you imagine this skill being used?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2865:- \"What would a user say that should trigger this skill?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2866:- \"Where should I create this skill? A `scripts/rotate_pdf.py` script would be helpful to store in the skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2884:Example: When designing a `frontend-webapp-builder` skill for queries like \"Build me a todo app\" or \"Build me a dashboard to track my steps,\" the analysis shows:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2887:2. An `assets/hello-world/` template containing the boilerplate HTML/React project files would be helpful to store in the skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2889:Example: When building a `big-query` skill to handle queries like \"How many users have logged in today?\" the analysis shows:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2892:2. A `references/schema.md` file documenting the table schemas would be helpful to store in the skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2894:To establish the skill's contents, analyze each concrete example to create a list of the reusable resources to include: scripts, references, and assets.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2898:At this point, it is time to actually create the skill.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2900:Skip this step only if the skill being developed already exists. /home/jbb/.codex/skills/screen-content-planner/SKILL.md\"`\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3387:description: Turn one product analysis card, implementation plan, UX analysis, or equivalent planning artifact into a complete screen-content plan for future visual mockups. Use when Codex needs to determine which screens are needed, what each screen must contain, what app language, platform format, product wording, data, states, and missing information are required before a separate mockup-generation skill begins. Do not use for generating visual mockups, styling systems, image assets, or implementation code.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3396:This skill is the first step in a two-skill workflow:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3398:1. This skill defines screen scope, content, data, states, reuse constraints, and unresolved blockers.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3399:2. A later visual mockup skill turns the plan into mockups.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3429:5. **Map planned behavior.** Use the provided implementation or product plan to identify workflows, states, roles, data entities, edge cases, failure modes, and permission differences that need screen coverage.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3432:8. **Review wording for production readiness.** Ensure labels, headings, empty states, errors, CTAs, helper text, and status messages are written for end users, not developers or implementation teams.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3434:10. **Prepare the handoff.** End with a clean handoff note for the later visual mockup skill, without doing visual design work.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3456:Do not ask for visual style details such as color palette, typography, illustration direction, spacing, motion, or high-fidelity layout preferences. Those belong to the later mockup creation skill.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3464:Use wording that a real end user can understand in the application language. Avoid implementation wording, internal team shorthand, database names, component names, raw enum values, route names, debug labels, placeholder text, and developer instructions unless the product itself is for developers and the source explicitly requires that vocabulary.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3552:- Ensure every wording item is end-user-facing, in the application language, and free of development or implementation jargon.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3576:- Map the screen back to source requirements, workflows, implementation plan items, constraints, or acceptance criteria.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3604:- Which skill must use.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3606:- Which wording requirements or draft copy the mockup skill must preserve.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3617:- User-facing wording is production-ready, in the application language, and free of development jargon, -->\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4:Ici, on a besoin de créer un skill qui va prendre le résultat du skill qu'on avait créé qui s'appelle Screen Content Planner, corrigé d'une bloat analysis éventuellement. En tout cas, ça prend une description de skill et enfin, ça prend une description de screen, pardon, et ça les transforme en mock-up visuel. Ce que ça fait, c'est que si jamais c'est une technologie web, on les fait directement, en fait, quoi qu'il arrive, en fait, on les fait en HTML et CSS. Et il faut bien que le skill, avant de générer les screens, il fasse une analyse complète des styles avec les couleurs, les border radius. En fait, il faut réutiliser ce qu'il y a dans Frontend skill pour pouvoir faire une analyse du design qu'on a dans l'application pour que les mock-ups, ils soient cohérents avec ce qu'on a déjà dans l'application. Et ensuite, ce qu'il faut que ça fasse, c'est que ça, du coup, ça génère les fichiers HTML et CSS, le CSS séparé du HTML à chaque fois. Chaque screen, il est dans son fichier HTML et chaque fichier HTML, il a son fichier CSS. Et ensuite, ce qu'on fait, c'est qu'on render avec le format d'image correct qui correspond à ce qu'on est en train de faire. Donc, par exemple, si c'est une application mobile en mode portrait, il faut qu'on fasse un render dans du browser en 9 16e et qu'on fasse ensuite une capture d'image et qu'on construise un carrousel dans la carte pour pouvoir montrer tous les mock-ups dans un carrousel. C'est aussi important que dans le skill, il y ait les règles de formatting qu'on a pour décision OS. Et ça veut dire qu'à chaque fois, je veux que les outputs soient créés avec les règles de formatting. knowledge gap\n\n---\n\n## Prototype Phase 4: Domain Model\n\n### domain-modeler\n**Trigger**: `proto:domain` + `status:todo`\n**Output**: Domain Model wiki page, creates mockup issue, transitions to `complete`\n**Role**: Domain Analyst - define entities, state machines, business rules\n**Prompt Source**: Universal Prompt Pack `domain-business-logic.md`\n\n---\n\n## Prototype Phase 5: Mockup (UX/UI Specification)\n\n### mockup-designer\n**Trigger**: `proto:mockup` + `status:todo`\n**Output**: UX/UI Spec wiki page, transitions to `user_review`\n**Role**: UX/UI Spec Author - create reviewable specification\n**Prompt Source**: Universal Prompt Pack `ux-ui-spec.md`\n\n### mockup-reviser\n**Trigger**: `proto:mockup` + `status:user_review` + `hasFeedback` + no `approved` label\n**Output**: Updated specification, stays at `user_review`\n**Role**: Incorporate user feedback into UX/UI spec\n\n### mockup-validator\n**Trigger**: `proto:mockup` + `status:user_review` + `userApproved`\n**Output**: UX/UI Spec wiki page, creates architecture issue, transitions to `validated`\n**Role**: Finalize approved specification, advance pipeline\n\n---\n\n## Prototype Phase 6: Architecture\n\n### architect\n**Trigger**: `proto:architecture` + `status:todo`\n**Output**: Architecture wiki page, creates api_contracts issue, transitions to `complete`\n**Role**: System Architect - design components, interfaces, deployment\n**Prompt Source**: Universal Prompt Pack `system-architecture.md`\n\n---\n\n## Prototype Phase 7: API Contracts\n\n### api-designer\n**Trigger**: `proto:api_contracts` + `status:todo`\n**Output**: API Contracts wiki page, creates quality_ops issue, transitions to `complete`\n**Role**: Data and API Designer - define endpoints, schemas, data model\n**Prompt Source**: Universal Prompt Pack `data-api-contracts.md`\n\n---\n\n## Prototype Phase 8: Quality Ops\n\n### quality-ops-planner\n**Trigger**: `proto:quality_ops` + `status:todo`\n**Output**: Quality Ops wiki page, creates test_strategy issue, transitions to `complete`\n**Role**: Quality/Security/Ops Architect - security model, observability, runbooks\n**Prompt Source**: Universal Prompt Pack `quality-security-ops.md`\n\n---\n\n## Prototype Phase 9: Test Strategy\n\n### test-strategist\n**Trigger**: `proto:test_strategy` + `status:todo`\n**Output**: Test Strategy wiki page, creates delivery issue, transitions to `complete`\n**Role**: QA Lead - test pyramid, traceability matrix, release gates\n**Prompt Source**: Universal Prompt Pack `test-strategy.md`\n\n---\n\n## Prototype Phase 10: Delivery Plan\n\n### delivery-planner\n**Trigger**: `proto:delivery` + `status:todo`\n**Output**: Delivery Plan wiki page, creates redteam issue, transitions to `complete`\n**Role**: Delivery Planner - milestones, backlog, risk register\n**Prompt Source**: Universal Prompt Pack `delivery-plan.md`\n\n---\n\n## Prototype Phase 11: Red Team\n\n### redteam-reviewer\n**Trigger**: `proto:redteam` + `status:todo`\n**Output**: Red Team Report, verdict label, transitions to `verdict_rendered`\n**Role**: Red Team - adversarial review, find weaknesses\n**Prompt Source**: Universal Prompt Pack `redteam-design-review.md`\n\n**Verdicts**:\n- `verdict:ship` - Ready for implementation\n- `verdict:revise` - Needs targeted fixes\n- `verdict:block` - Major rework required\n\n### sdd-initiator\n**Trigger**: `proto:redteam` + `status:verdict_rendered` + `verdictShip`\n**Output**: Creates SDD issue, closes redteam\n**Role**: Bridge from red team approval to SDD packaging\n\n---\n\n## Prototype Phase 12: SDD (System Design Document)\n\n### design-packager\n**Trigger**: `proto:sdd` + `status:todo`\n**Output**: SDD wiki page, Requirement\n\n- Do not end a turn with a dirty `git status`.\n- By the end of the turn, the repository must be clean.\n- If code changed, you must end the turn with a proper git commit unless the operator explicitly says not to commit.\n- If documentation or design/spec artifacts changed as part of the requested work, those changes must also be committed before ending the turn unless the operator explicitly says not to commit.\n- A proper commit means:\n  - the commit message reflects the real intent of the staged diff\n  - the staged diff matches a coherent unit of work\n  - relevant verification has been run when feasible before commit\n- Do not treat leftover changes as safely \"unrelated\" by default. Assume they may be unfinished work from a prior turn.\n- If the tree is already dirty, you must perform a reconciliation step before committing:\n  - inspect the existing changes\n  - analyze their intent\n  - decide whether they belong in the current unit of work or a separate one\n  - ensure the final commit structure respects that intent\n- If reconciliation reveals multiple intents, use separate commits rather than one mixed commit unless the operator explicitly requests otherwise.\n- Do not end a code-changing turn with uncommitted changes without explicitly stating why that was unavoidable.\n\n\n## JavaScript REPL (Node)\n- Use `js_repl` for Node-backed JavaScript with top-level await in a persistent kernel.\n- `js_repl` is a freeform/custom tool. Direct `js_repl` calls must send raw JavaScript tool input (optionally with first-line `// codex-js-repl: timeout_ms=15000`). Do not wrap code in JSON (for example `{\"code\":\"...\"}`), quotes, or markdown code fences.\n- Helpers: `codex.tmpDir`, `codex.tool(name, args?)`, and `codex.emitImage(imageLike)`.\n- `codex.tool` executes a normal tool call and resolves to the raw tool output object. Use it for shell and non-shell tools alike. Nested tool outputs stay inside JavaScript unless you emit them explicitly.\n- `codex.emitImage(...)` adds one image to the outer `js_repl` function output each time you call it, so you can call it multiple times to emit multiple images. It accepts a data URL, a single `input_image` item, an object like `{ bytes, mimeType }`, or a raw tool response object with exactly one image and no text. It rejects mixed text-and-image content.\n- Example of sharing an in-memory Playwright screenshot: `await codex.emitImage({ bytes: await page.screenshot({ type: \"jpeg\", quality: 85 }), mimeType: \"image/jpeg\" })`.\n- Example of sharing a local image tool result: `await codex.emitImage(codex.tool(\"view_image\", { path: \"/absolute/path\" }))`.\n- When encoding an image to send with `codex.emitImage(...)` or `view_image`, prefer JPEG at about 85 quality when lossy compression is acceptable; use PNG when transparency or lossless detail matters. Smaller uploads are faster and less likely to hit size limits.\n- Top-level bindings persist across cells. If a cell throws, prior bindings remain available and bindings that finished initializing before the throw often remain usable in later cells. For code you plan to reuse across cells, prefer declaring or assigning it in direct top-level statements before operations that might throw. If you hit `SyntaxError: Identifier 'x' has already been declared`, first reuse the existing binding, reassign a previously declared `let`, or pick a new descriptive name. Use `{ ... }` only for a short temporary block when you specifically need local scratch names; do not wrap an entire cell in block scope if you want those names reusable later. Reset the kernel with `js_repl_reset` only when you need a clean state.\n- Top-level static import declarations (for example `import x from \"./file.js\"`) are currently unsupported in `js_repl`; use dynamic imports with `await import(\"pkg\")`, `await import(\"./file.js\")`, or `await import(\"/abs/path/file.mjs\")` instead. Imported local files must be ESM `.js`/`.mjs` files and run in the same REPL VM context. Bare package imports always resolve from REPL-global search roots (`CODEX_JS_REPL_NODE_MODULE_DIRS`, then cwd), not relative to the imported file location. Local files may statically import only other local relative/absolute/`file://` `.js`/`.mjs` files; package and builtin imports from local files must stay dynamic. `import.meta.resolve()` returns importable strings such as `file://...`, bare package names, and `node:...` specifiers. Local file modules reload between execs, while top-level bindings persist until `js_repl_reset`.\n- Avoid direct access to `process.stdout` / `process.stderr` / `process.stdin`; it can corrupt the JSON line protocol. Use `console.log`, `codex.tool(...)`, and `codex.emitImage(...)`.\n\n## Skills\nA skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. This skill should be used when users want to create a new skill (or update an existing skill) that extends Codex's capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, or tool integrations.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:750:  short-description: Create or update a skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:755:This skill provides guidance for creating effective skills.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:795:You may use subagents during iteration to validate whether a skill works on realistic tasks or whether a suspected problem is real. This is most useful when you want an independent pass on the skill's behavior, outputs, or failure modes after a revision.  Only do this when it is possible to start new subagents.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:797:When using subagents for validation, treat that as an evaluation surface. The goal is to learn whether the skill generalizes, not whether another agent can reconstruct the answer from leaked context.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:803:Every skill consists of a required SKILL.md file and optional bundled resources:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:806:skill-name/\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:813:│   └── openai.yaml - UI metadata for skill lists and chips\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:824:- **Frontmatter** (YAML): Contains `name` and `description` fields. These are the only fields that Codex reads to determine when the skill gets used, thus it is very important to be clear and comprehensive in describing what the skill is, and when it should be used.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:825:- **Body** (Markdown): Instructions and guidance for using the skill. Only loaded AFTER the skill triggers (if at all).\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:829:- UI-facing metadata for skill lists and chips\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:831:- Create: human-facing `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt` by reading the skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:832:- Generate deterministically by passing the values as `--interface key=value` to `scripts/generate_openai_yaml.py` or `scripts/init_skill.py`\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:857:- **Avoid duplication**: Information should live in either SKILL.md or references files, not both. Prefer references files for detailed information unless it's truly core to the skill—this keeps SKILL.md lean while making information discoverable without hogging the context window. Keep only essential procedural instructions and workflow guidance in SKILL.md; move detailed reference material, schemas, and examples to references files.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:863:- **When to include**: When the skill needs files that will be used in the final output\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:870:A skill should only contain essential files that directly support its functionality. Do NOT create extraneous documentation or auxiliary files, including:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:878:The skill should only contain the information needed for an AI agent to do the job at hand. It should not contain auxiliary context about the process that went into creating it, setup and testing procedures, user-facing documentation, etc. Creating additional documentation files just adds clutter and confusion.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:885:2. **SKILL.md body** - When skill triggers (<5k words)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:890:Keep SKILL.md body to the essentials and under 500 lines to minimize context bloat. Split content into separate files when approaching this limit. When splitting out content into other files, it is very important to reference them from SKILL.md and describe clearly when to read them, to ensure the reader of the skill knows they exist and when to use them.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:892:**Key principle:** When a skill supports multiple variations, frameworks, or options, keep only the core workflow and selection guidance in SKILL.md. Move variant-specific details (patterns, examples, configuration) into separate reference files.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:918:bigquery-skill/\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:929:Similarly, for skills supporting multiple frameworks or variants, organize by variant:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:972:1. Understand the skill with concrete examples\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:973:2. Plan reusable skill contents (scripts, references, assets)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:974:3. Initialize the skill (run init_skill.py)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:975:4. Edit the skill (implement resources and write SKILL.md)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:976:5. Validate the skill (run quick_validate.py)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:977:6. Iterate based on real usage and forward-test complex skills.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:987:- Name the skill folder exactly after the skill name.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:991:Skip this step only when the skill's usage patterns are already clearly understood. It remains valuable even when working with an existing skill.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:993:To create an effective skill, clearly understand concrete examples of how the skill will be used. This understanding can come from either direct user examples or generated examples that are validated with user feedback.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:995:For example, when building an image-editor skill, relevant questions include:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:997:- \"What functionality should the image-editor skill support? Editing, rotating, anything else?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:998:- \"Can you give some examples of how this skill would be used?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:999:- \"I can imagine users asking for things like 'Remove the red-eye from this image' or 'Rotate this image'. Are there other ways you imagine this skill being used?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1000:- \"What would a user say that should trigger this skill?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1001:- \"Where should I create this skill? If you do not have a preference, I will place it in `$CODEX_HOME/skills` (or `~/.codex/skills` when `CODEX_HOME` is unset) so Codex can discover it automatically.\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1005:Conclude this step when there is a clear sense of the functionality the skill should skill-creator\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2605:description: Guide for creating effective skills. This skill should be used when users want to create a new skill (or update an existing skill) that extends Codex's capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, or tool integrations.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2607:  short-description: Create or update a skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2620:This skill provides guidance for creating effective skills.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2660:You may use subagents during iteration to validate whether a skill works on realistic tasks or whether a suspected problem is real. This is most useful when you want an independent pass on the skill's behavior, outputs, or failure modes after a revision.  Only do this when it is possible to start new subagents.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2662:When using subagents for validation, treat that as an evaluation surface. The goal is to learn whether the skill generalizes, not whether another agent can reconstruct the answer from leaked context.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2668:Every skill consists of a required SKILL.md file and optional bundled resources:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2671:skill-name/\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2678:│   └── openai.yaml - UI metadata for skill lists and chips\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2689:- **Frontmatter** (YAML): Contains `name` and `description` fields. These are the only fields that Codex reads to determine when the skill gets used, thus it is very important to be clear and comprehensive in describing what the skill is, and when it should be used.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2690:- **Body** (Markdown): Instructions and guidance for using the skill. Only loaded AFTER the skill triggers (if at all).\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2694:- UI-facing metadata for skill lists and chips\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2696:- Create: human-facing `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt` by reading the skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2697:- Generate deterministically by passing the values as `--interface key=value` to `scripts/generate_openai_yaml.py` or `scripts/init_skill.py`\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2722:- **Avoid duplication**: Information should live in either SKILL.md or references files, not both. Prefer references files for detailed information unless it's truly core to the skill—this keeps SKILL.md lean while making information discoverable without hogging the context window. Keep only essential procedural instructions and workflow guidance in SKILL.md; move detailed reference material, schemas, and examples to references files.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2728:- **When to include**: When the skill needs files that will be used in the final output\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2735:A skill should only contain essential files that directly support its functionality. Do NOT create extraneous documentation or auxiliary files, including:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2743:The skill should only contain the information needed for an AI agent to do the job at hand. It should not contain auxiliary context about the process that went into creating it, setup and testing procedures, user-facing documentation, etc. Creating additional documentation files just adds clutter and confusion.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2750:2. **SKILL.md body** - When skill triggers (<5k words)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2755:Keep SKILL.md body to the essentials and under 500 lines to minimize context bloat. Split content into separate files when approaching this limit. When splitting out content into other files, it is very important to reference them from SKILL.md and describe clearly when to read them, to ensure the reader of the skill knows they exist and when to use them.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2757:**Key principle:** When a skill supports multiple variations, frameworks, or options, keep only the core workflow and selection guidance in SKILL.md. Move variant-specific details (patterns, examples, configuration) into separate reference files.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2783:bigquery-skill/\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2794:Similarly, for skills supporting multiple frameworks or variants, organize by variant:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2837:1. Understand the skill with concrete examples\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2838:2. Plan reusable skill contents (scripts, references, assets)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2839:3. Initialize the skill (run init_skill.py)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2840:4. Edit the skill (implement resources and write SKILL.md)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2841:5. Validate the skill (run quick_validate.py)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2842:6. Iterate based on real usage and forward-test complex skills.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2852:- Name the skill folder exactly after the skill name.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2856:Skip this step only when the skill's usage patterns are already clearly understood. It remains valuable even when working with an existing skill.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2858:To create an effective skill, clearly understand concrete examples of how the skill will be used. This understanding can come from either direct user examples or generated examples that are validated with user feedback.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2860:For example, when building an image-editor skill, relevant questions include:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2862:- \"What functionality should the image-editor skill support? Editing, rotating, anything else?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2863:- \"Can you give some examples of how this skill would be used?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2864:- \"I can imagine users asking for things like 'Remove the red-eye from this image' or 'Rotate this image'. Are there other ways you imagine this skill being used?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2865:- \"What would a user say that should trigger this skill?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2866:- \"Where should I create this skill? If you do not have a preference, I will place it in `$CODEX_HOME/skills` (or `~/.codex/skills` when `CODEX_HOME` is unset) so Codex can discover it automatically.\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2870:Conclude this step when there is a clear sense of the functionality the skill should support.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2874:To turn concrete examples into an effective skill, analyze each example by:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2879:Example: When building a `pdf-editor` skill to handle queries like \"Help me rotate this PDF,\" the analysis shows:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2882:2. A `scripts/rotate_pdf.py` script would be helpful to store in the skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2884:Example: When designing a `frontend-webapp-builder` skill for queries like \"Build me a todo app\" or \"Build me a dashboard to track my steps,\" the analysis shows:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2887:2. An `assets/hello-world/` template containing the boilerplate HTML/React project files would be helpful to store in the skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2889:Example: When building a `big-query` skill to handle queries like \"How many users have logged in today?\" the analysis shows:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2892:2. A `references/schema.md` file documenting the table schemas would be helpful to store in the skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2894:To establish the skill's contents, analyze each concrete example to create a list of the reusable resources to include: scripts, references, and assets.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2898:At this point, it is time to actually create the skill.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2900:Skip this step only if the skill being developed already exists. In this case, continue to the next step.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2902:Before running `init_skill.py`, ask where the user wants the skill created. If they do not specify a location, default to `$CODEX_HOME/skills`; when `CODEX_HOME` is unset, fall back to `~/.codex/skills` so the skill is auto-discovered.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2904:When creating a new skill from scratch, always run the `init_skill.py` script. The script conveniently generates a new template skill directory that automatically includes everything a skill requires, making the skill creation process much more efficient and reliable.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2909:scripts/init_skill.py <skill-name> --path <output-directory> [--resources scripts,references,assets] [--examples]\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2915:scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path \"${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2916:scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path \"${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills\" --resources scripts,references\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2917:scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path ~/work/skills --resources scripts --examples\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2922:- Creates the skill directory at the specified path\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2930:Generate `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt` by reading the skill, then pass them as `--interface key=value` to `init_skill.py` or regenerate with:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2933:scripts/generate_openai_yaml.py <path/to/skill-folder> --interface key=value\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2940:When editing the (newly-generated or existing) skill, remember that the skill is being created for another instance of Codex to use. Include information that would be beneficial and non-obvious to Codex. Consider what procedural knowledge, domain-specific details, or reusable assets would help another Codex instance execute these tasks more effectively.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2942:After substantial revisions, or if the skill is particularly tricky, you should use subagents to forward-test the skill on realistic tasks or artifacts. When doing so, pass the artifact under validation rather than your diagnosis of what is wrong, and keep the prompt generic enough that success depends on transferable reasoning rather than hidden ground truth.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2946:To begin implementation, start with the reusable resources identified above: `scripts/`, `references/`, and `assets/` files. Note that this step may require user input. For example, when implementing a `brand-guidelines` skill, the user may need to provide brand assets or templates to store in `assets/`, or documentation to store in `references/`.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2950:If you used `--examples`, delete any placeholder files that are not needed for the skill. Only create resource directories that are actually required.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2960:- `name`: The skill name\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2961:- `description`: This is the primary triggering mechanism for your skill, and helps Codex understand when to use the skill.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2964:  - Example description for a `docx` skill: \"Comprehensive document creation, editing, and analysis with support for tracked changes, comments, formatting preservation, and text extraction. Use when Codex needs to work with professional documents (.docx files) for: (1) Creating new documents, (2) Modifying or editing content, (3) Working with tracked changes, (4) Adding comments, or any other document tasks\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2970:Write instructions for using the skill and its bundled resources.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2974:Once development of the skill is complete, validate the skill folder to catch basic issues early:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2977:scripts/quick_validate.py <path/to/skill-folder>\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2984:After testing the skill, you may detect the skill is complex enough that it requires forward-testing; or users may request improvements.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2986:User testing often this happens right after using the skill, with fresh context of how the skill performed.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2990:1. Use the skill on real tasks\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2998:To forward-test, launch subagents as a way to stress test the skill with minimal context.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2999:Subagents should *not* know that they are being asked to test the skill. A later visual mockup skill turns the plan into mockups.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3107:5. **Map planned behavior.** Use the provided implementation or product plan to identify workflows, states, roles, data entities, edge cases, failure modes, and permission differences that need screen coverage.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3110:8. **Review wording for production readiness.** Ensure labels, headings, empty states, errors, CTAs, helper text, and status messages are written for end users, not developers or implementation teams.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3112:10. **Prepare the handoff.** End with a clean handoff note for the later visual mockup skill, without doing visual design work.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3134:Do not ask for visual style details such as color palette, typography, illustration direction, spacing, motion, or high-fidelity layout preferences. itself is for developers and the source explicitly requires that vocabulary.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3230:- Ensure every wording item is A later visual mockup skill turns the plan into mockups.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3429:5. **Map planned behavior.** Use the provided implementation or product plan to identify workflows, states, roles, data entities, edge cases, failure modes, and permission differences that need screen coverage.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3432:8. **Review wording for production readiness.** Ensure labels, headings, empty states, errors, CTAs, helper text, and status messages are written for end users, not developers or implementation teams.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3434:10. **Prepare the handoff.** End with a clean handoff note for the later visual mockup skill, without doing visual design work.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3456:Do not ask for visual style details such as color palette, typography, illustration direction, spacing, motion, or high-fidelity layout preferences. This skill should be used when users want to create a new skill (or update an existing skill) that extends Codex's capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, or tool integrations.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:259:  short-description: Create or update a skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:264:This skill provides guidance for creating effective skills.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:304:You may use subagents during iteration to validate whether a skill works on realistic tasks or whether a suspected problem is real. This is most useful when you want an independent pass on the skill's behavior, outputs, or failure modes after a revision.  Only do this when it is possible to start new subagents.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:306:When using subagents for validation, treat that as an evaluation surface. The goal is to learn whether the skill generalizes, not whether another agent can reconstruct the answer from leaked context.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:312:Every skill consists of a required SKILL.md file and optional bundled resources:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:315:skill-name/\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:322:│   └── openai.yaml - UI metadata for skill lists and chips\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:333:- **Frontmatter** (YAML): Contains `name` and `description` fields. These are the only fields that Codex reads to determine when the skill gets used, thus it is very important to be clear and comprehensive in describing what the skill is, and when it should be used.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:334:- **Body** (Markdown): Instructions and guidance for using the skill. Only loaded AFTER the skill triggers (if at all).\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:338:- UI-facing metadata for skill lists and chips\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:340:- Create: human-facing `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt` by reading the skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:341:- Generate deterministically by passing the values as `--interface key=value` to `scripts/generate_openai_yaml.py` or `scripts/init_skill.py`\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:366:- **Avoid duplication**: Information should live in either SKILL.md or references files, not both. Prefer references files for detailed information unless it's truly core to the skill—this keeps SKILL.md lean while making information discoverable without hogging the context window. Keep only essential procedural instructions and workflow guidance in SKILL.md; move detailed reference material, schemas, and examples to references files.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:372:- **When to include**: When the skill needs files that will be used in the final output\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:379:A skill should only contain essential files that directly support its functionality. Do NOT create extraneous documentation or auxiliary files, including:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:387:The skill should only contain the information needed for an AI agent to do the job at hand. It should not contain auxiliary context about the process that went into creating it, setup and testing procedures, user-facing documentation, etc. Creating additional documentation files just adds clutter and confusion.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:394:2. **SKILL.md body** - When skill triggers (<5k words)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:399:Keep SKILL.md body to the essentials and under 500 lines to minimize context bloat. Split content into separate files when approaching this limit. When splitting out content into other files, it is very important to reference them from SKILL.md and describe clearly when to read them, to ensure the reader of the skill knows they exist and when to use them.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:401:**Key principle:** When a skill supports multiple variations, frameworks, or options, keep only the core workflow and selection guidance in SKILL.md. Move variant-specific details (patterns, examples, configuration) into separate reference files.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:427:bigquery-skill/\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:438:Similarly, for skills supporting multiple frameworks or variants, organize by variant:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:481:1. Understand the skill with concrete examples\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:482:2. Plan reusable skill contents (scripts, references, assets)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:483:3. Initialize the skill (run init_skill.py)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:484:4. Edit the skill (implement resources and write SKILL.md)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:485:5. Validate the skill (run quick_validate.py)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:486:6. Iterate based on real usage and forward-test complex skills.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:496:- Name the skill folder exactly after the skill name.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:500:Skip this step only when the skill's usage patterns are already clearly understood. It remains valuable even when working with an existing skill.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:502:To create an effective skill, clearly understand concrete examples of how the skill will be used. This understanding can come from either direct user examples or generated examples that are validated with user feedback.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:504:For example, when building an image-editor skill, relevant questions include:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:506:- \"What functionality should the image-editor skill support? I have enough context. The thread reply will say plainly that `AGENTS.md` did not block correct formatting; the failure was my missing precedence rule between exact-token backticks and conceptual bold.

# AGENT
<!-- decision-os:note {"id":"note-agent-1783611357049-fb211896","timestamp":"2026-07-09T15:35:57.049Z"} -->

## A. What I Did

1. I removed the earlier **bold-at-the-start** pattern because that turned numbered items into fake subtitles.
2. I moved bold into sentences and used it for phrases I judged to carry the main meaning, such as **deep engineering completeness review**, **fundamental missing tasks**, **engineering completeness**, and **checkbox traceability**.
3. I used backticks mainly for obvious literal outputs and exact names, such as `ready`, `blocked`, report section names, and file paths.
4. That produced the imbalance you identified: too many conceptual words became bold, while too few exact planning terms became backticked.

---

## B. Why The Rule Did Not Force The Right Result

1. `AGENTS.md` says bold is for **important words that carry the point**, but it does not define a density limit, a per-sentence maximum, and a priority rule against backticks.
2. `AGENTS.md` says backticks are for `technical`, `secondary`, `exact`, and `literal` terms, but it does not classify this skill's planning vocabulary.
3. I used the wrong heuristic: **important concept** became bold first, then only code-shaped literals became backticked.
4. The better heuristic is the reverse: exact contract terms get backticks first, conceptual emphasis gets bold second, ordinary nouns stay plain.

---

## C. Correct Logic For This Skill

1. Use backticks for exact workflow tokens: `task-dependency`, `implementation-orchestrator`, `input card`, `report card`, `ready`, `blocked`, `group ids`, `task ids`, `source card ids`, and report section names.
2. Use bold for conceptual load-bearing ideas: **deep engineering completeness review**, **fundamental missing tasks**, **checkbox traceability**, and **planning completeness**.
3. Leave normal domain words plain when they are not literal output fields, exact statuses, paths, config keys, commands, routes, ids, and code symbols.

---

## D. Answer

1. The `AGENTS.md` rule did allow correct formatting.
2. The problem was that I applied it without a precedence rule between **semantic emphasis** and `exact-token marking`.
3. No card content was changed in this answer.
